description: The key insight is that persistent homology — the backbone of topological data analysis — provides a natural framework for quantum error correction. Each bar in a persistence barcode corresponds to a topological feature that persists across scales, and these persistent features ARE the logical qubits of a topological quantum code. Conjecture: For any simplicial complex K, the first persistent homology bar with birth time epsilon and death time delta defines a quantum error-correcting code with distance d >= delta/epsilon and rate k/H_1(K). The barcode IS the code specification: birth times give stabilizer generators, death times give code distance. Why now: the surface code is just H_1 of a grid, and its distance equals the longest bar in the barcode. This generalizes immediately. Test: construct the barcode code for the torus (distance 4, rate 1/9) and verify it matches the toric code. Prove the distance bound for arbitrary complexes. Impact: every dataset with persistent topology becomes a quantum code, and the barcode distance theorem gives a systematic way to construct new codes from topology.
proof_strategy: Define the barcode code B(K) for a simplicial complex K: qubits = vertices, stabilizers = boundary maps of 1-simplices, logical operators = persistent 1-cycles. Prove: (1) the stabilizer group is Abelian and squares to identity, (2) the code distance equals the ratio delta/epsilon where epsilon and delta are birth and death of the longest bar, (3) the code rate equals dim(H_1(K))/|V(K)|. Test: for K = square lattice on torus, verify distance = min(L,W) and rate = 1/N matching the toric code.
title: Topological Quantum Error Correction from Homological Persistence

description: The key insight is that protein folding minimizes a topological energy: the persistent homology barcode of the protein's contact map. The native fold of a protein is the configuration that minimizes the total persistence of the contact filtration. Conjecture: The native state of a protein P minimizes sum_i (d_i - b_i) over all possible 3D configurations, where {b_i, d_i} is the persistent homology barcode of the distance matrix of P's C-alpha atoms. Why now: AlphaFold2 showed that contact maps are sufficient for structure prediction, but it used deep learning without understanding WHY contact maps work. Persistent homology provides the mathematical reason: the barcode captures the topological constraints (no self-intersection, hydrophobic core, etc.) that determine the fold. Test: compute the barcode for 100 proteins from the PDB and verify that the native fold has lower total persistence than 1000 random decoy folds for each protein. Impact: protein folding becomes a topological optimization problem with a provably unique minimum, explaining why folding is fast and reliable despite Levinthal's paradox.
proof_strategy: Define the contact filtration for protein P with N residues: for distance threshold t, build the Vietoris-Rips complex R_t from the pairwise C-alpha distances. Compute the persistent homology barcode PH(P, configuration) = {(b_i, d_i)}. Define TotalPersistence(P) = sum_i (d_i - b_i). Conjecture: the native fold minimizes TotalPersistence over all valid configurations. Test: for each of 100 PDB proteins, generate 1000 decoy configurations using Rosetta, compute TotalPersistence for each, and verify the native fold has the minimum. Prove that TotalPersistence is a Lyapunov function for folding dynamics in the simplified HP model.
title: Biological Topology: Protein Folding as Persistent Homology Optimization

description: The Riemann zeta function zeta(s) has non-trivial zeros at s = 1/2 + i*gamma_n on the critical line (assuming RH). These zeros encode deep arithmetic information. Conjecture: the zeros gamma_n are the spectrum of a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space, and this operator is the Casimir element of a quantum group G_q. Specifically, define the 'zeta quantum group' G_q as the q-deformation of SU(2) where q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} (using the first zero gamma_1 ~ 14.13). The Casimir element C_q of G_q has eigenvalues that are quadratic functions of the representation labels, and the spectrum of C_q is {n(n+1) : n in N}. Conjecture: the Riemann zeros gamma_n are related to the spectrum of C_q by gamma_n = f(spectrum(C_q)) for some function f. If f is linear, this would mean the zeros are evenly spaced, which is false (the zeros have Poisson-like spacings). If f is logarithmic, gamma_n ~ pi*n/log(n) which matches the average spacing. Conjecture: the spectral statistics of C_q match the GUE random matrix statistics of the Riemann zeros (Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture). Test: compute the spectrum of C_q for G_q with q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} and compare the spectral statistics with the Riemann zeros. Impact: the Riemann hypothesis is a representation-theoretic statement about quantum groups.
proof_strategy: Define the quantum group SU_q(2) with q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} where gamma_1 ~ 14.13 is the first Riemann zero. The representation theory: irreducible representations V_n of dimension n+1 for n = 0, 1, 2, .... The Casimir element C_q acts on V_n with eigenvalue [n]_q * [n+1]_q where [m]_q = (q^m - q^{-m})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer. For q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1}: [m]_q = sin(m * pi * gamma_1) / sin(pi * gamma_1). The eigenvalues of C_q on V_n are: lambda_n = [n]_q * [n+1]_q = sin(n*pi*gamma_1) * sin((n+1)*pi*gamma_1) / sin(pi*gamma_1)^2. Conjecture: the set {lambda_n : n >= 1} encodes the Riemann zeros in a way that preserves their statistical properties. Specifically, the level spacings {lambda_{n+1} - lambda_n} should follow the GUE distribution (Wigner-Dyson surmise). Test: compute lambda_n for n = 1..1000, compute the level spacings, and compare with the GUE distribution P(s) = (32/pi^2) * s^2 * exp(-4*s^2/pi^2). Also compare with the Riemann zero spacings. This requires numerical computation of q-deformed representations.
title: Quantum Groups from Number Theory: The Riemann Hypothesis as a Representation Problem

proof_strategy: For n <= 2, B_n is respectively a point or a segment, so the clique-face property is immediate. For n = 3, two permutation vertices are adjacent exactly when their quotient permutation has a single nontrivial cycle; every nonidentity element of S_3 has this property, so the 1-skeleton of B_3 is complete on six vertices. However B_3 is 4-dimensional and its facets are given by equations x_ij = 0, each containing only four permutation vertices, so a five-vertex clique is not the vertex set of any face. Thus B_3 fails the property. For n >= 3, B_n contains a face isomorphic to B_3 by fixing n-3 rows and columns to the corresponding identity entries. Since the clique-face property passes to faces, B_n also fails it.
title: Birkhoff polytopes have the clique-face property only in dimensions n <= 2

description: Let G be a topological group and H ≤ G a dense subgroup with the subspace topology. If H is extremely amenable, meaning every continuous action of H on a nonempty compact Hausdorff space has a fixed point, then G is extremely amenable. This isolates the density step used when passing from the automorphism group of a projective Fraisse limit to the closure subgroup of the homeomorphism group of the quotient continuum.
domain_bridges: projective Fraisse limits to homeomorphism groups
combinatorial Ramsey properties to fixed point properties of compact flows
dense automorphism groups to closed homeomorphism groups
proof_strategy: Given a continuous G-action on a nonempty compact Hausdorff space X, restrict it to the dense subgroup H. Extreme amenability of H gives x ∈ X fixed by every h ∈ H. For arbitrary g ∈ G, the orbit map a ↦ a • x is continuous, and the equalizer of this map with the constant map a ↦ x is closed in G because X is Hausdorff. This closed set contains the dense subset H, hence is all of G. Therefore g • x = x for every g ∈ G.
title: Extreme amenability passes from a dense subgroup to its ambient topological group

description: For every finite K5-free simple graph G on n vertices, assign weight 1/2 to every edge contained in a triangle and weight 1 to every other edge. Then G has a bipartition whose monochromatic edge-weight is at most n^2/16. Equivalently, deleting edges of total such weight at most n^2/16 always makes G bipartite. The balanced complete 4-partite graph shows that the constant 1/16 would be best possible.
domain_bridges: Translates a Ramsey-Turan style forbidden-clique problem into a weighted max-cut inequality.
Extends the paper's weighted K4-free triangle-discounted cut result to the next clique size K5.
Connects Sudakov-type bipartization bounds with edge weights determined by local clique membership.
proof_strategy: A plausible route is to combine a weighted Turan symmetrization argument with a stability analysis for near-extremal K5-free graphs. First show that an extremal counterexample may be assumed to have a bounded number of vertex types under weighted twin-symmetrization. Then reduce the resulting finite weighted optimization problem to complete multipartite templates plus sparse exceptional triangle-free structure. The complete 4-partite template gives the extremal value n^2/16, while triangle-free exceptional parts should be controlled by known max-cut lower bounds for triangle-free graphs.
title: Weighted K5-free max-cut conjecture with triangle-discounted edges

description: Conjecture: Let A and B be reduced arrangements of d projective complex lines in P^2 with d <= 9. If their central intersection lattices are isomorphic, their Milnor algebras S/J_f and S/J_g have the same Hilbert function in every degree, and mdr(f) = mdr(g), then the minimal graded free resolutions of S/J_f and S/J_g have identical graded Betti numbers. Equivalently, there is no Ziegler pair of at most nine lines satisfying both conditions (HF) and (MDR).
domain_bridges: intersection lattices of line arrangements as rank-3 matroids
Jacobian ideals and Milnor algebras as graded modules over C[x,y,z]
Hilbert functions versus graded Betti tables of minimal free resolutions
minimal Jacobian syzygy degree as the initial degree of the logarithmic derivation module
proof_strategy: Formalize line arrangements by products of pairwise non-proportional homogeneous linear forms in C[x,y,z]. Define the intersection lattice combinatorially via the induced rank-3 matroid, and define the Milnor algebra, Hilbert function, mdr, and graded Betti numbers algebraically. For d < 9, use the paper's small-degree rigidity theorem together with a finite verification of the remaining Betti possibilities. For d = 9, reduce to the finite list of realizable rank-3 matroids on nine elements and verify, by certified Gröbner-basis computations over algebraic parameter strata, that every pair with equal Hilbert function and equal mdr has the same graded Betti table.
title: No HF-MDR Ziegler pairs with at most nine lines

description: Conjecture: Every connected locally finite multigraph G admits a rooted tree-cut decomposition (T,V) into finite bags, of finite adhesion, which is componental and linked, displays every end of G bijectively as an end of T, and is degree-normalized as follows. If a tree-end alpha of T displays the graph end omega, and e_n is the nth adhesion edge on the root-to-alpha ray of T, then: (i) if the edge-degree of omega is a finite natural number d, then |F_{e_n}| = d for all sufficiently large n; (ii) if the edge-degree of omega is infinite, then for every k : Nat, |F_{e_n}| >= k for all sufficiently large n. This strengthens the paper's displayed-edge-degree conclusion by asking for eventual exact stabilization along finite-degree ends and divergence along infinite-degree ends.
domain_bridges: Freudenthal-style end theory for locally finite graphs
Lean formalization of finite cuts via Finset edge sets
withTop Nat formulation of finite versus infinite edge-degree
rooted tree rays as sequences indexed by Nat
proof_strategy: Start from the linked componental finite-adhesion decomposition given by the paper for locally finite graphs. Refine the construction along each displayed tree ray by choosing nested finite edge-cuts that are minimal representatives of the corresponding end whenever the end has finite edge-degree, using edge-Menger to maintain linkedness after contractions/refinements. For infinite-degree ends, diagonalize over k and choose the nth sufficiently far cut to have size at least k, again preserving componentality by taking the end-side component and preserving linkedness via the minimum-cut characterization of the linked condition. The main technical point is a simultaneous refinement argument over all tree rays that does not destroy previously normalized adhesion values.
title: Degree-normalized linked tree-cut decompositions for locally finite graphs

description: For every finite-dimensional vector space E over a finite field F and every rank r with 0 <= r <= dim E, the map sending a sparse-paving q-matroid M of rank r on E to its set of r-dimensional circuit-hyperplanes is a bijection onto the stable sets of the q-Johnson graph J_q(E,r), whose vertices are r-dimensional subspaces and whose edges join pairs with intersection dimension r-1. Equivalently, a set S of r-subspaces defines a sparse-paving q-matroid precisely when any two distinct members of S intersect in dimension at most r-2.
domain_bridges: sparse-paving q-matroids to independent sets in the q-Johnson graph
finite vector-space submodule lattice to graph-theoretic stable sets
proof_strategy: Formalize q-matroids by rank functions on the submodule lattice satisfying the q-matroid rank axioms. Define paving and sparse-paving in terms of circuit dimensions and dual paving, or equivalently by the circuit-hyperplane characterization. Prove first that in any sparse-paving q-matroid, two distinct r-dimensional circuit-hyperplanes cannot meet in dimension r-1, since their sum would violate the sparse-paving circuit elimination/dual-paving condition. Conversely, given a stable set S of r-subspaces, define a rank function by declaring subspaces contained in members of S to have the expected ranks, declaring members of S to be dependent hyperplanes of rank r-1, and all other r-subspaces to be bases; then extend by truncation to all subspaces. Verify the rank axioms R1-R3 by splitting on dimensions below r, equal to r, and above r, using the stable-set intersection bound for the only nontrivial submodularity case. Show the two constructions are inverse.
title: Sparse-paving q-matroids are exactly stable sets in the q-Johnson graph

description: Let p and q be distinct primes. Suppose P,Q ∈ ℕ[x] are generating polynomials for two dice with no 0-labeled sides, with P(1)=p^2 and Q(1)=q^2, and whose sum-frequency polynomial equals that of two standard pq-sided dice: P Q = (x + x^2 + ⋯ + x^(pq))^2. Then P and Q must be one of exactly three explicit pairs, indexed by c=0,1,2: with G(n,s)=∑_{i=0}^{n-1} x^(s i), the p^2-sided die is x·G(p,1)^(2-c)·G(p,q)^c and the q^2-sided die is x·G(q,1)^c·G(q,p)^(2-c).
domain_bridges: Cyclotomic polynomial divisibility translates dice relabeling into factor allocation among irreducible factors.
The explicit polynomials G(p,1) and G(p,q) encode rectangular decompositions of labels modulo p and q.
Nonnegative polynomial factorization over ℕ can be reduced to uniqueness of factorization over ℤ plus evaluation at x=1.
proof_strategy: First rewrite the standard pq-sided die polynomial as x·G(p,1)·G(q,p)=x·G(q,1)·G(p,q). Over ℤ[x], use unique factorization and the cyclotomic decomposition x+⋯+x^(pq)=x Φ_p Φ_q Φ_pq. Since Φ_p(1)=p, Φ_q(1)=q, and Φ_pq(1)=1, the condition P(1)=p^2 forces P/x to contain exactly two Φ_p factors and no Φ_q factors; only the exponent c∈{0,1,2} of Φ_pq remains free. The complementary factor goes to Q. Finally identify the three resulting products with the explicit nonnegative polynomials using Φ_p Φ_pq=G(p,q) and Φ_q Φ_pq=G(q,p).
title: Prime-product square-sided dice have exactly three relabeling types

description: Let p > 5 be prime, and let mu(p) be the least positive integer m such that 2^m ≡ 1 or -1 mod p. The conjecture is that there are infinitely many primes p for which mu(p) = (p - 1) / 2. By the projective-doubling classification in the paper, this is equivalent to saying that infinitely many prime odd bases attain the maximal possible terminal four-digit Kaprekar cycle length (p - 1) / 2.
domain_bridges: Kaprekar digit dynamics to multiplication by 2 on projective residue classes
terminal cycle length to projective multiplicative order modulo p
extremal cycle length to Artin-type primitive root phenomena
proof_strategy: First formalize the paper's equivalence: for prime p > 5, the longest terminal four-digit Kaprekar cycle in base p has length (p - 1) / 2 iff the least m > 0 with 2^m = ±1 in ZMod p is (p - 1) / 2. Then prove that infinitely many primes satisfy this modular condition. A sufficient route is Artin's primitive root conjecture for 2, since if 2 is a primitive root modulo p then the projective order of 2 is exactly (p - 1) / 2. Conditional proofs could be obtained from Hooley's GRH-dependent theorem; an unconditional Lean proof would require major analytic number theory beyond current mathlib.
title: Infinitely many extremal prime odd bases for four-digit Kaprekar dynamics

description: For any inner form G of GL_n over a non-archimedean local field F, the Hochschild homology of the Braverman-Kazhdan asymptotic Hecke algebra J(G) is canonically isomorphic to the Hochschild homology of the classical Hecke algebra C_c^∞(G), and the Kazhdan-Lusztig bijection on Bernstein components appears in this isomorphism. Concretely, for each Bernstein component s indexed by an inertial equivalence class, the summand HH_*(J(G))_s is identified with HH_*(C_c^∞(G))_s via the map induced by the natural inclusion of Schwartz functions, and this identification is compatible with the Kazhdan-Lusztig bijection between Bernstein components and certain data on the dual side. This conjecture is established in the paper for inner forms of GL_n; the grand challenge extension to all connected reductive p-adic groups remains open.
proof_strategy: The isomorphism HH_*(J(G)) ≅ HH_*(C_c^∞(G)) for inner forms of GL_n is established via Bushnell-Kutzko and Sécherre-Stevens type theory, which provides explicit decompositions of both algebras into tensor products of spherical Hecke algebras of types and intertwining algebras. The key step is showing that the type-theoretic decompositions of J(G) and C_c^∞(G) have matching Hochschild homology because their type-theoretic factors have isomorphic Hochschild homology (via the Paley-Wiener theorem and the explicit formulas in terms of reductive centralizers of L-parameters). For a Lean formalization, one would first define J(G) and C_c^∞(G) as algebras over Q̄_ℓ, define Hochschild homology of such algebras, establish the type-theoretic decompositions, and then prove the isomorphism by reducing to the type-level comparison.
title: Hochschild homology isomorphism between asymptotic and classical Hecke algebras for inner forms of GL_n

description: For every fixed integer k ≥ 3, the Conformability problem is NP-complete when restricted to connected d-regular graphs G of odd order n with independence number α(G) = k and maximum degree d ≥ n/2. The paper establishes this for k = 3 by reduction from perfect triangle packing in K₄-free graphs. The conjecture asserts that hardness persists for all larger independence numbers, where the complement graph has clique number k and conformable color classes correspond to cliques of odd size up to k in the complement, requiring richer packing structures to encode NP-hard problems.
proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's reduction by constructing, for each k ≥ 3, a family of connected d-regular graphs with α(G) = k and d ≥ n/2 whose conformability encodes exact clique-packing problems in K_{k+1}-free complements. For odd k, conformable color classes map to cliques of sizes 1,3,...,k in G̅; for even k, to cliques of sizes 1,3,...,k-1. The key challenge is designing gadgets that force the correct distribution of clique sizes in any conformable coloring, generalizing the triangle-packing enforcement at k=3. A reduction from exact cover by k-sets or k-clique packing in K_{k+1}-free graphs would establish hardness.
title: Conformability remains NP-complete for all fixed independence numbers at least 3

description: For every gentle tree algebra A = KQ/<R> of finite global dimension, let Ω_A be the finite set of indecomposable A-modules, equivalently the permissible arcs in the modified surface model. For S ⊆ Ω_A, let cl_A(S) be the set of indecomposable summands lying in the resolving subcategory generated by S together with the projective modules. The conjecture is that cl_A is a convex-geometry closure operator: in particular, it satisfies anti-exchange. Explicitly, if C is resolving-closed, x and y are distinct indecomposables not in C, and x ∈ cl_A(C ∪ {y}), then y ∉ cl_A(C ∪ {x}). This is finite, falsifiable by computation on gentle trees, and would imply that the poset of resolving subcategories of a gentle tree algebra is meet-distributive.
domain_bridges: resolving subcategories as finite closure systems
indecomposable string modules as arcs in a surface model
tilting modules as maximal compatible arc configurations
anti-exchange closure operators and convex geometries
proof_strategy: Formalize the modified surface model for a gentle tree algebra as finite combinatorial data: arcs, projective arcs, and the forcing rules generated by extensions and kernels of epimorphisms. Prove that the resolving closure computed by these local forcing rules is a closure operator. Then prove anti-exchange by induction on the number of vertices of the underlying tree, removing a leaf and checking the finitely many local configurations involving the adjacent relation. The key combinatorial lemma should show that if adding an arc y forces a new arc x over a closed set C, then the unique minimal chain of local forcings from y to x is oriented by the tree order and cannot be reversed without already forcing y from C.
title: Anti-exchange for resolving closure in gentle tree algebras

description: Conjecture: Let G be a finite simple connected regular graph of odd order. If every independent set of G has size at most 2, then G is conformable if and only if G is complete. Equivalently, in the zero-deficiency odd regular regime, the NP-hardness threshold α(G)=3 from the paper is sharp with respect to independence number: no non-complete graph with α(G)≤2 can be conformable.
domain_bridges: regular odd graphs imply zero deficiency, so conformability requires every color class to have odd cardinality
proper color classes are independent sets, so α(G)≤2 forces every odd color class to be a singleton
using Δ(G)+1 singleton color classes forces Δ(G)+1=|V(G)|, hence G is complete
proof_strategy: For a regular graph, the deficiency sum is 0. Since |V(G)| is odd, a conformable coloring must have every one of its Δ(G)+1 color classes odd, including excluding empty classes. Proper color classes are independent sets. Under α(G)≤2, each color class has size at most 2, so an odd nonempty color class must have size 1. Thus a conformable coloring partitions V(G) into singleton classes and therefore uses exactly |V(G)| colors. Since the coloring has Δ(G)+1 colors, Δ(G)+1=|V(G)|, so Δ(G)=|V(G)|-1, which implies G is complete. Conversely, an odd complete graph is conformable by coloring each vertex with its own color.
title: Alpha-two sharpness for conformability in odd regular graphs

description: For every positive integer k ≥ 1 and every positive integer n ≥ 1, every k-restricted characteristic sequence of a permutation on Z_n is the score sequence of some k-tournament on n vertices. Here, a characteristic sequence c(φ) of a permutation φ ∈ S_n is the non-decreasing arrangement of the multiset {i + φ(i) : i ∈ Z_n}, and it is k-restricted if each value in this multiset appears at most k times. A k-tournament on n vertices is a complete directed multigraph where each pair of vertices is connected by exactly k arcs, and its score sequence is the non-decreasing sequence of vertex outdegrees. This conjecture unifies the Bebeacua et al. conjecture (k=1: binary xrays, where each value appears at most once, correspond to 1-tournament score sequences) and the Brualdi–Fritscher conjecture (k=2: unrestricted xrays, where each value appears at most twice, correspond to 2-tournament score sequences).
proof_strategy: Proceed by induction on k. The base case k=1 (Bebeacua et al.) and case k=2 (Brualdi–Fritscher) would require constructing explicit injections from k-restricted characteristic sequences to k-tournament score sequences using the transitive tournament decomposition introduced in the paper. For the inductive step, leverage the construction that builds a k-tournament from a permutation: given a (k+1)-restricted characteristic sequence, decompose it into a k-restricted subsequence and an additional layer, construct the k-tournament by induction, then extend via the transitive tournament decomposition to obtain a (k+1)-tournament with the desired score sequence. The key difficulty is verifying Landau-type conditions for the constructed sequences at each stage.
title: Generalized Xray-Tournament Correspondence Conjecture

description: For any dimension n ≥ 2, among all n-dimensional orthogonal flat tori of unit volume, the equilateral torus (with all lattice side lengths equal) uniquely maximizes the zeta regularized determinant of the Laplacian. Formally, if T_l = ℝⁿ/(l₁ℤ × ⋯ × lₙℤ) with ∏lᵢ = 1 and lᵢ > 0, then det_ζ(Δ_{T_l}) ≤ det_ζ(Δ_{T_eq}) with equality if and only if l₁ = ⋯ = lₙ = 1, where T_eq is the equilateral torus. This validates Sarnak's conjecture in the orthogonal setting.
proof_strategy: Express the zeta regularized determinant on an orthogonal torus in terms of Epstein-type zeta functions of the lattice. Show log-concavity of the determinant as a function of the logarithmic side-length parameters using the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality and convexity properties of the Epstein zeta function. The unique maximizer follows from strict concavity of the log-determinant functional on the simplex of unit-volume configurations.
title: The Equilateral Torus Uniquely Maximizes the Zeta Regularized Determinant Among Orthogonal Flat Tori of Unit Volume

description: For every integer t ≥ 1, the natural density c_t := lim_{N→∞} (1/N) #{0 ≤ n < N : s₂(n+t) ≥ s₂(n)} strictly exceeds 1/2, with the explicit quantitative bound c_t ≥ 1/2 + 2^{-2s₂(t)-1}, where s₂(m) counts the ones in the binary expansion of m. This was Cusick's long-standing conjecture, recently resolved via first-exit medians for principal subsequence ideals after an exact deconvolution replacing the distribution of s₂(n+t)−s₂(n) by a finite stopped random-walk law.
proof_strategy: Formalize the probability measure μ_t on ℤ giving the density of values of s₂(n+t)−s₂(n), proving its existence via the 2-adic structure of carry propagation. Develop the exact deconvolution identity that replaces μ_t by a finite stopped random-walk distribution indexed by the block structure of t in binary. Then formalize the first-exit median inequality for principal subsequence ideals to extract the quantitative bias 2^{-2s₂(t)-1}, combining the random-walk representation with the combinatorics of binary addition carries.
title: Cusick's sum-of-digits conjecture with explicit bias bound

description: For integers n ≥ 2k and k ≥ 3, any two non-trivial cross-intersecting families A, B ⊆ ([n] choose k) satisfy |A| * |B| ≤ h(n,k)^2, where h(n,k) = choose(n-1, k-1) - choose(n-k-1, k-1) + 1 is the size of the Hilton-Milner family. This formalizes the resolved Frankl-Wang conjecture.

Apply the shifting technique to reduce to left-compressed families, and use the diversity method to bound the sizes of families with elements far from a common core. Establish properties of the extended shift operation to manage the inductive steps.
title: Sharp Product Bound for Non-Trivial Cross-Intersecting Families

description: Let $a_k$ denote the number of Pólya trees on $k$ nodes, and define $\omega_k = \sum_{d \mid k} d \cdot a_d$. Then $a_1 = 1$ and for all $k \ge 2$: $a_k = \frac{1}{k-1} \sum_{j=1}^{k-1} a_j \, \omega_{k-j}$. This is derived by extracting coefficients from the logarithmic derivative of the Pólya functional equation $A(z) = z \exp(A(z)) \Phi(z)$, where $[z^k] \sum_{i \ge 1} z^i A'(z^i) = \omega_k$.
proof_strategy: Define the OGF A(z) via the Pólya functional equation A(z) = z·exp(A(z))·Φ(z) where Φ(z) = exp(∑_{i≥2} A(z^i)/i). Take the logarithmic derivative to obtain zA'(z) = A(z)(1 + ∑_{i≥1} z^i A'(z^i)). Extract the coefficient of z^k on both sides: the left side gives k·a_k; the right side gives a_k + ∑_{j=1}^{k-1} a_j·ω_{k-j}, where ω_k arises from the identity [z^k]∑_{i≥1} z^i A'(z^i) = ∑_{d|k} d·a_d. Rearranging yields the recurrence. The Lean formalization should first establish the coefficient extraction identity for the divisor sum, then apply it to the differentiated functional equation.
title: Pólya tree coefficient divisor-sum recurrence

description: For any binary delta-matroid $D$ on ground set $E$ and any twuality operator $\bullet \in \{\ast, \times, \ast\times, \times\ast, \ast\times\ast\}$, the sequence of coefficients of the partial-$\bullet$ polynomial $^{\partial}w_{D}^{\bullet}(z) = \sum_{A \subseteq E} z^{w(D^{\bullet \mid A})}$ is log-concave. This conjecture extends the interpolation property established in the paper (which implies the sequence has no internal zeros) and directly parallels the resolution of the Mason-Welsh conjecture for matroid independent sets.

title: Log-concavity of Partial-Twuality Polynomials for Binary Delta-Matroids

description: Let R be any commutative ring and G any finite group. Define HH₀(R[G]) as the quotient of the group algebra R[G] by the R-submodule spanned by all additive commutators xy - yx. The canonical R-linear map sending a basis element g of R[G] to the conjugacy class of g descends to an R-linear equivalence HH₀(R[G]) ≃ R[Conj(G)]. Equivalently, the only relations in degree-zero Hochschild homology of a finite group algebra identify conjugate group elements.

Zeroth Hochschild homology as the cocenter of an algebra
Conjugacy classes as the finite analogue of orbital data appearing in Hecke algebra cocenters
A Lean-formalizable stepping stone toward the paper's comparison of Hochschild homology for asymptotic and compactly supported Hecke algebras

For the inverse, define a map on conjugacy classes by sending the class of g to the image of the basis vector g in the commutator quotient. This is well-defined because hgh⁻¹ - g equals the commutator δ_h δ_{g h⁻¹} - δ_{g h⁻¹} δ_h in R[G]. Extend linearly and check the two composites on basis generators.
title: HH0 of a finite group algebra is the free module on conjugacy classes

description: For every real ε > 0, there exists N such that every finite simple graph G on n ≥ N vertices with minimum degree at least (5/8 + ε)n has an edge-decomposition into 5-cycles whenever G is C5-divisible, i.e. every vertex has even degree and 5 divides the number of edges. This is the remaining small odd-cycle case suggested by the generalized Nash-Williams threshold δ_{C_ℓ} = ℓ/(2ℓ−2), after the triangle case and the long odd-cycle cases addressed in the paper.
proof_strategy: Formalize finite simple graphs, edge sets, vertex degrees, and C5-decompositions as a finite family of subgraphs each isomorphic to a 5-cycle whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint and cover E(G). The mathematical proof would likely combine an absorption framework with approximate C5-decompositions and a stability analysis around the known extremal obstruction giving the lower bound 5/8. In Lean, the conjecture can initially be stated using abstract predicates `IsFiveCycle` and `HasC5Decomposition`, then refined to concrete cycle embeddings into `SimpleGraph`.
title: Asymptotic C5-decomposition threshold equals 5/8

description: Let A₁ and A₂ be central hyperplane arrangements over Q of the same rank with isomorphic intersection lattices L(A₁) ≅ L(A₂). For all primes p at which both arrangements admit good reduction, the local ask zeta functions coincide: Z^{ask}_{A₁/Z_p}(T) = Z^{ask}_{A₂/Z_p}(T). This extends the well-known combinatorial invariance conjecture for Igusa local zeta functions to the ask zeta function setting, motivated by the paper's construction recovering ask zeta functions from the Igusa local zeta function of the cone and the truncated flag Hilbert-Poincaré series. The conjecture asserts that the arithmetic content entering through the substitution in the flag Hilbert-Poincaré series is nevertheless determined by the intersection lattice for good reduction primes.
proof_strategy: Exploit the paper's main result that local ask zeta functions are recovered by substitutions in the truncated flag Hilbert-Poincaré series. Prove that (1) the truncated flag Hilbert-Poincaré series of A is determined by L(A), (2) the substitution parameters for primes of good reduction depend only on the isomorphism type of L(A) and the residue field size q, and (3) the matrix of linear forms constructed from A yields the same ask zeta function as any other arrangement with isomorphic lattice. The key difficulty is showing that the matrix construction and the substitution are both lattice-determined, which may require developing a lattice-theoretic characterization of the associated matroid and its representability constraints.
title: Combinatorial Invariance of Ask Zeta Functions for Hyperplane Arrangements

description: For every n ≥ 1, there exists a finite family C of pairwise disjoint open bounded convex sets in R^{3n} such that the space L of line transversals to C is homotopy equivalent to S^{n-1}. This strengthens the authors' theorem (which proves only H̃_{n-1}(L) ≠ 0) and formalizes their stated belief that the transversal spaces they construct have the homotopy type of a sphere.
proof_strategy: The authors already construct explicit families of convex sets and show nontrivial homology via a quotient/retraction argument onto a configuration space identified with a product of spheres. To upgrade H̃_{n-1}(L) ≠ 0 to a full homotopy equivalence L ≃ S^{n-1}, one would need to show that the natural retraction map from L onto a subspace homeomorphic to S^{n-1} is a homotopy equivalence—likely by establishing that the fiber of this retraction is contractible (a deformation retraction argument) or by computing all homotopy groups directly. The key geometric step is controlling the higher connectivity of the transversal space relative to its (n-1)-dimensional core.
title: Homotopy type of the line transversal space equals S^{n-1}

description: In Theorem 1.2 of the paper, the function $f(n,s')$ bounding the size of the separator can be chosen to be $ns'-1$ when the vertex sets in $\mathcal{A}$ are pairwise disjoint.
proof_strategy: Apply Menger's theorem to the union of the sets in $\mathcal{A}$ and the branch vertices of $W$. If no separator of size $ns'-1$ exists, there are $ns'$ disjoint paths, which can be distributed among the $n$ disjoint sets and then routed to distinct nails of a subwall.
title: Optimal Separator Bound for Wall Connectors

description: For a number field F with r₁ real embeddings and r₂ pairs of complex conjugate embeddings, and for every integer n ≥ 2, the bottom-degree Betti-Whittaker periods of a generic cohomological automorphic representation π of GLₙ over F and its contragredient π∨ satisfy p^b(π∨) = (-1)^{b(F,n)} · p^b(π), where b(F,n) = r₁·⌊n²/4⌋ + r₂·n(n-1)/2 is the bottom cohomological degree. This removes the regularity assumptions in Chen's earlier result and extends the contragredient period relation to the full class of generic cohomological representations.
proof_strategy: The proof requires: (1) formalizing the bottom cohomological degree formula b(F,n) = r₁⌊n²/4⌋ + r₂·n(n-1)/2 and proving its parity properties; (2) constructing the Betti-Whittaker period as a pairing between relative Lie algebra cohomology and Whittaker models; (3) establishing the duality isomorphism on cohomology induced by the contragredient map on representations; (4) computing the sign incurred by the contragredient action on the bottom-degree cohomology, which reduces to tracking how the Chevalley involution acts on the lowest weight vector of the coefficient system and how this interacts with the Whittaker functional. Key intermediate lemma: the sign equals (-1)^b because the contragredient reverses the orientation of the flag variety contributing exactly b mod 2 sign changes.
title: Contragredient Period Sign Formula for Betti-Whittaker Periods of GL(n)

description: An infinite word $x_1x_2\dots \in \mathcal{A}^\mathbb{N}$ can be realized as the $(-\beta)$-expansion of some $x \in I_\beta$ if and only if for all $n \ge 1$, the suffix $x_n x_{n+1} \dots$ is less than or equal to $d^*(0, -\beta)$ in the alternating lexicographic order. The alternating lexicographic order $\preceq$ is defined such that $x \preceq y$ if either $x=y$ or at the first index $k$ where they differ, $x_k < y_k$ when $k$ is odd and $x_k > y_k$ when $k$ is even.
proof_strategy: Define the alternating lexicographic order on infinite sequences, the $(-\beta)$-transformation $T_{-\beta}$, and the sequence $d^*(0, -\beta)$. Prove that the shift space defined by this order condition is invariant and corresponds exactly to the admissible sequences of the $(-\beta)$-transformation, mirroring Parry's proof for positive $\beta$-expansions.
title: Ito-Sadahiro Admissibility Condition for Negative Beta-Expansions

description: For a real quadratic field K with discriminant Δ₀, dimension d in its AFMY tower, and conductor f dividing f₀(d), the excess e = [K^{fd} : K_L^{d;f}] equals 1 if and only if gcd(f, d) = 1. This characterizes when the Kopp-Lagarias ray class field K_L^{d;f} coincides with the standard ray class field K^{fd}, and is the key structural ingredient in the paper's thesis that SIC overlap units factor into Stark units from these fields.
proof_strategy: First formalize the Kopp-Lagarias ray class field construction K_L^{d;f} as a subfield of K^{fd} defined via non-maximal orders with conductor f in the ring of integers of K. Then compute the degree [K^{fd} : K_L^{d;f}] using class field theory, showing it equals the generalized Euler totient Φ_K(gcd(f,d)). The excess equals 1 iff this degree is trivial, i.e., gcd(f,d)=1. The key step uses that the norm map on the ray class group modulo fd surjects onto the ray class group of the non-maximal order with conductor f precisely when f and d are coprime.
title: Excess-One Criterion for Kopp-Lagarias Ray Class Fields

description: A left-regular bipartite graph of degree d is an s-optimal small-set expander (i.e., every subset X of left vertices of size t ≤ s has exactly d * t distinct neighbors, maximizing expansion) if and only if its girth is at least 2s + 2. This bridges the combinatorial property of girth with the expansion parameter α_G(t) and the optimality of the associated code B(G).
proof_strategy: The forward direction assumes a cycle of length 2k ≤ 2s and shows that the k left vertices on the cycle must share neighbors, reducing the neighborhood size below dk and violating optimality. The backward direction assumes a subset X of left vertices of size t ≤ s with shared neighbors and constructs a cycle of length ≤ 2s, contradicting the girth assumption.
title: Girth-Expansion Equivalence for Optimal Small-Set Expanders

description: The cluster algebra structure on the coordinate ring of a partial flag variety G/P, defined via the restriction of the base affine space cluster structure, is isomorphic to the cluster algebra structure defined on the corresponding Schubert cell via the double Bruhat cell cluster structure.
proof_strategy: Construct a sequence of mutations that maps the initial seed of the Schubert cell cluster structure to the initial seed of the partial flag variety cluster structure, and verify that the cluster variables and exchange relations are preserved under this transformation, thereby establishing a cluster algebra isomorphism.
title: Isomorphism of Cluster Structures on Schubert Cells and Partial Flag Varieties

description: For every integer t >= 1, the natural density c_t = lim_{N->∞} (1/N) * #{0 <= n < N : s_2(n+t) >= s_2(n)} satisfies c_t >= 1/2 + 2^{-2*s_2(t)-1}.
proof_strategy: exact deconvolution replaced by finite stopped random-walk law and first-exit median analysis
title: Explicit bias lower bound for the density of n with s_2(n+t) >= s_2(n)

description: For any finite family of convex splinters in d-dimensional Euclidean space, if the intersection of every subfamily of size at most 2d+1 is non-empty, then the intersection of the entire family is non-empty. This extends the classical Helly's theorem to the more general structure of convex splinters.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definition of a convex splinter as a union of convex sets satisfying the affine independence condition. Proceed by induction on the dimension d, adapting the original proof by Arocha, Bracho, and Montejano which leverages Radon's theorem and properties of affine dependence on splinters.
title: Helly's Theorem for Convex Splinters

description: For all positive integers s' and t', there exist integers t and f such that for any graph G, vertex set A, and wall W of size at least t, either there exists a vertex set X of size at most f separating A from the branch vertices of W, or there exists a subwall W' of W of size at least t' and s' vertex-disjoint A-W'-paths ending in distinct nails of W'.
proof_strategy: Formalize walls, subwalls, branch vertices, nails, and vertex separators in Lean. Establish Menger's Theorem as a baseline. Construct the subwall W' by analyzing the connectivity from A to the branch vertices of W, and apply the paper's arguments to find the disjoint paths ending in distinct nails.
title: Wall-Menger Theorem

description: Let $A(z)$ be the ordinary generating series of Pólya trees, with coefficients $a_n$, and let $\rho$ be its radius of convergence such that $A(\rho) = 1$. Then for all integers $k \ge 1$ and all real numbers $t$ such that $0 \le t < \rho$, the truncation error of the $k$-th partial sum is bounded by $0 \le A(t) - \sum_{i=1}^k a_i t^i \le \frac{(t/\rho)^{k+1}}{1 - t/\rho}$.
proof_strategy: Define the Pólya tree generating function $A(z)$ and its radius of convergence $\rho$. Establish the bound $a_k \le \rho^{-k}$ from the fact that $A(\rho) = 1$. Use this coefficient bound to dominate the tail of the series by a geometric series, yielding $\sum_{i \ge k+1} a_i t^i \le \sum_{i \ge k+1} (t/\rho)^i = \frac{(t/\rho)^{k+1}}{1 - t/\rho}$.
title: Pólya Tree Generating Series Taylor Approximation Error Bound

description: For any connected reductive group $G$ defined over a number field $F$, and any cohomological generic automorphic representation $\pi$ of $G(\mathbb{A}_F)$, the ratio of the Betti-Whittaker periods $\Omega(\pi^\vee) / \Omega(\pi)$ is an algebraic number, generalizing the explicit relation established for $\mathrm{GL}(n)$ where the ratio is a specific power of $i$ depending on the bottom degree $b = r_1 \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor + r_2 n(n-1)/2$.
proof_strategy: Generalize the definition of Betti-Whittaker periods to arbitrary connected reductive groups using relative Lie algebra cohomology and Franke's theorem. Show that the contragredient map on cohomology acts by an algebraic scalar on the bottom-degree Whittaker cohomology classes, leveraging the algebraicity of the Whittaker functionals and the action of the Chevalley involution.
title: Algebraicity of Contragredient Betti-Whittaker Period Ratio for Reductive Groups

catalog_references: Paper: definition of S_K = Herm_2(O_K) with quadratic form 2 det
Paper: use of S_K(2N) as the Neron-Severi lattice of Picard-rank-four K3 surfaces
description: Conjecture: Let d < 0 be squarefree, let K = Q(√d), and let O_K have Z-basis {1, ω}, where ω = √d if d ≠ 1 mod 4 and ω = (1 + √d)/2 if d ≡ 1 mod 4. Form the rank-four lattice S_K = Herm_2(O_K) with quadratic form q(A) = 2 det(A), and use the basis given by the two diagonal Hermitian matrix units together with the off-diagonal elements 1 and ω. Then the determinant of the Gram matrix of the associated integral symmetric bilinear form is exactly the fundamental discriminant D_K: det Gram(S_K) = d if d ≡ 1 mod 4, and det Gram(S_K) = 4d otherwise.
domain_bridges: Identifies the discriminant of the rank-four K3 Neron-Severi lattice used in the paper with the field discriminant of K
Connects Hermitian matrix models for Bianchi groups to explicit integral quadratic forms
Provides a Lean-checkable arithmetic invariant underlying the congruence-level phenomena in the automorphism groups
proof_strategy: Choose the standard Z-basis of Herm_2(O_K): the two diagonal basis vectors and the two off-diagonal basis vectors corresponding to 1 and ω. Write z = x + yω. Since q([[a,z],[conj z,c]]) = 2ac - 2 Norm(z), the Gram matrix splits as a hyperbolic plane with determinant -1 and a rank-two negative norm block. If Tr(ω)=T and Norm(ω)=n, the norm block has matrix [[-2, -T], [-T, -2n]], whose determinant is 4n - T^2 = -D_K. Multiplying by the hyperbolic determinant -1 gives det Gram(S_K)=D_K.
title: Discriminant of the Hermitian Bianchi lattice S_K

description: Every connected, twin-free Cayley digraph of a finite abelian group of odd order is stable; that is, the automorphism group of its direct product with the complete digraph K_2 is isomorphic to the direct product of their individual automorphism groups.
proof_strategy: Formalize the direct product of digraphs, stability, and the twin-free property. Prove that an unstable connected digraph must admit an involutory automorphism that swaps twins. Show that for a Cayley digraph of an abelian group of odd order, the existence of such an automorphism forces the existence of an element of order 2 in the group, which contradicts Lagrange's theorem for groups of odd order.
title: Stability of Cayley Digraphs of Abelian Groups of Odd Order

description: For a finite acyclic quiver Q with longest path length n-1, the T-ideal of the principal subalgebra 𝔽Q≥1 is generated by the standard polynomial S = ∑_{σ∈S_n} x_{σ(1)}x_{σ(2)}...x_{σ(n)}.
proof_strategy: Show that S vanishes on the T-ideal and that every element of the T-ideal is a scalar multiple of S.
title: Symmetrized Monomial Generates T-Ideal in Acyclic Path Algebras

description: For every binary delta-matroid and every nontrivial twuality operator $ ullet \in \{\ast, \times, \ast\times, \times\ast, \ast\times\ast\}$, the partial-$\bullet$ polynomial $^\partial w_D^\bullet(z)$ is either even, odd, or both even-interpolating and odd-interpolating.
proof_strategy: Formalize delta-matroids and binary delta-matroids over a finite ground set, define the five twuality operators (twist, loop complementation, and their compositions), and construct the partial-twuality polynomial using the width function. Establish the parity and interpolation properties of the polynomial coefficients by analyzing how the twuality operators transform the feasible sets of a binary delta-matroid.
title: Binary Delta-Matroid Partial-Twuality Interpolation

description: For any bounded prism (A, I) where A/I is a regular local ring of dimension d, the restriction functor from the category of prismatic F-crystals on Spec(A/I) to the category of prismatic F-crystals on the punctured spectrum Spec(A/I) \ {m} is an equivalence of categories. This extends the paper's primitive purity theorem for Frobenius modules to the full setting of prismatic F-crystals, and would imply that the canonical F-isocrystal from Ogus's conjecture is uniquely determined by its restriction to any dense open subscheme.
proof_strategy: Reduce to the primitive purity theorem for Frobenius modules via the prismatic p-adic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence, showing that prismatic F-crystals on the punctured spectrum correspond to p-adic local systems that extend, then transport the purity result back through the equivalence. Key step: establish that the prismatic Riemann-Hilbert functor commutes with restriction to opens and preserves the Frobenius structure needed for the extension.
title: Prismatic Purity for F-Crystals on Regular Schemes

description: For any connected polymatroid $P$ and any element $e$, the set of indices $j \in \{0, \dots, f(e)\}$ for which the $j$-th slice-projection of $e$ is connected forms a contiguous interval of integers. This conjecture strengthens the paper's theorem that no two consecutive slice-projections can both be disconnected, and naturally generalizes the interval property trivially satisfied by matroids (where the rank $f(e) \le 1$).
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction that there exist indices $j < k < l$ such that the $j$-th and $l$-th slice-projections are connected, but the $k$-th is disconnected. Use the submodularity of the polymatroid rank function and the lattice of flats to demonstrate that if $P^{(k)}$ is disconnected by a partition $(A, B)$, then either $P^{(j)}$ or $P^{(l)}$ must also be disconnected by a related partition, contradicting the initial assumption.
title: Interval Property for Connected Slice-Projections of Polymatroids

description: Conjecture that for every integer k≥3 there exists a critical edge density γ_k∈(0,1) such that for all sufficiently large n, any graph on n vertices with edge density at least γ_k that contains no induced copy of K_{1,k} is ε n^2-close (in edit distance) to the complement of a complete (k−1)-partite graph whose part sizes differ by at most o(n) from the balanced partition n/(k−1).
proof_strategy: Stability via flag algebra computations combined with a removal lemma for induced stars
title: Typical (k−1)-partite complement structure of dense K_{1,k}-free graphs above the critical density

description: For every prime p ≥ 7 with p ≡ 3 mod 4, the determinant of the truncated Legendre-symbol matrix with polynomial parameter X is exactly ((p - 2) / 3)^2 X over ℤ[X]. Explicitly, for m = (p - 5) / 2 and matrix A indexed by Fin m with A_{j,k} = X + (j - k | p), where the Legendre symbol is viewed as an integer coefficient polynomial, det A = ((p - 2) / 3)^2 X.
domain_bridges: quadratic characters over finite fields to integer-valued polynomial matrices
Legendre-symbol Toeplitz matrices to determinant identities
finite linear algebra and principal minor reductions
proof_strategy: Formalize the matrix over Polynomial ℤ indexed by Fin ((p - 5) / 2). Prove the identity by importing or separately formalizing the inverse-data reduction from the full Chapman matrix C = [legendreSym p (j - i)] indexed by Fin ((p + 1) / 2). The determinant computation then reduces to Jacobi complementary minor identities and the rank-one determinant lemma for adding the constant X matrix. The remaining arithmetic simplification is Nat division: floor((p - 2) / 3) is represented by (p - 2) / 3.
title: Lean-formalizable Sun truncated Legendre-symbol determinant

description: A coordinate-symmetric r-coloring of the cube [t]^n is line-free with respect to combinatorial lines having at most K active coordinates if and only if the induced coloring of the discrete simplex Δ(t-1, n) has no monochromatic corner tuple of width at most K. This equivalence reduces checking line-freeness of a symmetric coloring (a property of the exponentially large cube) to checking corner-tuple-freeness on the polynomially-sized simplex, and is the theoretical foundation enabling the certified lower bounds HJ(3,3) ≥ 22 and HJ(4,2) ≥ 14.
proof_strategy: Formalize coordinate-symmetric colorings as functions on letter-count vectors (elements of the discrete simplex). Define corner tuples as the image of combinatorial lines under the letter-count map. The forward direction follows from the fact that a monochromatic line projects to a monochromatic corner tuple. The reverse direction uses the symmetry: if a corner tuple is monochromatic, the corresponding line (reconstructed by assigning active coordinates to the varying letter and fixed coordinates according to the count vector) is monochromatic in the original coloring by symmetry. The key invariant is that symmetric colorings factor through the letter-count projection.
title: Symmetric Coloring Reduction Lemma for Hales-Jewett Line-Freeness

description: For a totally real number field $k$, a prime $p$, and a subset $\Sigma$ of the $p$-adic primes of $k$, if $N_\infty/k$ is a $\Sigma$-ramified $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension (i.e., $N_\infty$ is contained in the maximal abelian pro-$p$-extension of $k$ unramified outside $\Sigma$), then the unramified Iwasawa module $X(N_\infty)$ is finite. This generalizes Greenberg's Conjecture from the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension to any $\Sigma$-ramified $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension.
proof_strategy: Extend the techniques of Greenberg's conjecture to $\Sigma$-ramified extensions by analyzing the $\mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$-module structure of $X(N_\infty)$ and using the restricted ramification conditions to bound the $\lambda$-invariant, potentially leveraging the new sufficient conditions provided in the paper.
title: Finiteness of Unramified Iwasawa Module for Sigma-Ramified Extensions

description: Fix rational transmission parameters θ,p with 0 < θ < 1 and 0 < p ≤ 1. For any two finite simple graphs G and H, let G □ H denote the Cartesian product and let Z_T^{θ,p}(G) be the minimum size of a θ-threshold, p-proportion transmission zero forcing set. Conjecture: Z_T^{θ,p}(G □ H) ≤ min(|V(H)| · Z_T^{θ,p}(G), |V(G)| · Z_T^{θ,p}(H)). This is falsifiable by a finite pair of graphs and rational parameters for which every initial set below the stated bound fails to fill the product.
domain_bridges: Transmission zero forcing as a weighted monotone cellular automaton on finite graphs
Cartesian graph products and layer-by-layer simulation arguments
Classical zero forcing product bounds adapted to fractional multi-neighbor forcing
proof_strategy: It should suffice to prove the first inequality Z_T(G □ H) ≤ |V(H)|·Z_T(G), since the second follows symmetrically. Let S be an optimal transmission zero forcing set of G. Initialize S × V(H) in G □ H. Simulate a successful transmission schedule for G simultaneously in every H-layer. At each simulated step, if u transmits to v in G, then for every h ∈ V(H), the vertex (u,h) transmits to (v,h). The extra Cartesian-product neighbors of (u,h) in the H-direction have first coordinate u and are already filled because the entire fiber over each filled vertex of G is filled. Hence the zero-forcing uniqueness condition and the transmitted weights in each layer match the original process on G. Induct over the finite successful schedule to show all vertices of V(G) × V(H) fill. The initialized set has cardinality |V(H)|·|S|. Repeat with the roles of G and H reversed and take the minimum.
title: Cartesian-product upper bound for transmission zero forcing

description: For any edge-colored graph G on n ≥ 3 vertices, if the minimum color degree δc(G) ≥ (n+1)/2, then the number of rainbow triangles rt(G) is at least f(n), where f(n) = (n^2-1)/8 if n is odd, f(n) = n^2/4 - 1 if n is even and n ≥ 6, and f(4) = 4.
proof_strategy: Formalize edge-colored graphs, minimum color degree, and rainbow triangles in Lean, then establish the lower bounds by analyzing the extremal graph structures and showing that any deviation from them strictly increases the number of rainbow triangles, proceeding by induction on n.
title: Exact minimum number of rainbow triangles with large minimum color degree

description: For a projective variety V of dimension n over F_1 with associated invertible Markov matrix A = Mk_1 ∈ GL_b(Z) (arising from the Markov endomorphism construction), the zeta function Z(V/F_1, t) = 1/det(I - tA) satisfies the Weil-type functional equation Z(V/F_1, 1/t) = ε · t^{-χ(V)} · Z(V/F_1, t), where ε ∈ {±1} and χ(V) = Σ_{i=0}^{2n} (-1)^i b_i is the topological Euler characteristic of V(C). This formalizes the paper's claim that the zeta function of V(F_1) satisfies all Weil conjectures except the Riemann hypothesis analog, using the bridge between F_1-geometry and the K-theory of Cuntz-Krieger algebras O_A.
proof_strategy: Reduce to computing det(I - tA) for the Markov matrix A = Mk_1 ∈ GL_b(Z) associated to V. The functional equation for Z(V/F_1, t) = 1/det(I - tA) follows from the identity det(I - (1/t)A) = det(-A/t) · det(I - tA^{-1})/det(A) combined with the constraint det(A) = 1^n = 1 (from det(Mk_q) = q^n evaluated at q = 1). The sign ε is determined by the determinant of A and the parity of χ(V). The K-theoretic computation of |V(F_{1^r})| via tr(ε_i^{π_i(1^r)}) in K_0(O_{A^r}) ⊕ K_1(O_{A^r}) provides the point-count interpretation linking to the Weil conjecture framework.
title: Functional Equation for F_1-Zeta Functions via Cuntz-Krieger Algebras

catalog_references: Lean mathlib: MvPolynomial, PowerSeries, Finsupp, Nat.Odd
description: Let Γ_R = R[p_1,p_3,p_5,...] and define the R-algebra endomorphism φ_t of Γ_R by φ_t(p_n) = (1 - t^n) p_n for every positive odd n. If Q_λ denotes the Schur Q-function indexed by a strict partition λ in the same vertex-operator normalization as the t=0 odd GJZ construction, and S^t_λ denotes the shifted t-Schur function obtained from the Fourier modes of the odd GJZ operator, then for every strict partition λ one has S^t_λ = φ_t(Q_λ). Equivalently, the shifted t-Schur family is obtained from the Schur Q basis by the odd plethystic substitution p_n ↦ (1 - t^n)p_n. This is falsifiable by coefficient comparison in the finite odd power-sum polynomial ring of degree at most |λ|.
domain_bridges: formal Laurent series identities ↔ polynomial algebra automorphisms
proof_strategy: Define the scaling algebra automorphism Φ_t on the odd power-sum ring by Φ_t(p_n) = (1 - t^n)p_n. Show coefficientwise that Φ_t ∂/∂p_n Φ_t⁻¹ = (1 - t^n)⁻¹ ∂/∂p_n. Therefore the odd GJZ field Y(z;t) is conjugate to the t=0 neutral-fermion field: Y(z;t) = Φ_t Y(z;0) Φ_t⁻¹. Since Φ_t fixes the vacuum vector 1, applying the negative Fourier modes indexed by a strict partition λ gives S^t_λ = Φ_t(S^0_λ) = Φ_t(Q_λ). In Lean, avoid infinite series by working degreewise in a truncated odd-variable polynomial algebra up to degree |λ|, then pass to the abstract graded Γ formulation.
title: Plethystic Triviality of the Shifted t-Schur Basis

description: For every finite connected simple graph G on n ≥ 2 vertices with unit edge resistances, let R_G be its effective-resistance matrix and define Δ(G) = (-1)^(n-1) det(R_G). Conjecture: 2^n (n-1) / n^n ≤ Δ(G) ≤ 2^(n-2) (n-1). Moreover, equality on the left holds exactly for the complete graph K_n, and equality on the right holds exactly for trees. This extends the Graham--Pollak tree determinant formula and predicts that adding simple edges monotonically decreases the signed resistance determinant down to the complete graph.
domain_bridges: spectral graph theory ↔ Euclidean distance matrices
Kirchhoff spanning tree theory ↔ determinant inequalities
effective resistance metrics ↔ Loewner order on graph Laplacians
proof_strategy: Formalize the resistance matrix through the Moore--Penrose inverse of the graph Laplacian or equivalently through Kirchhoff ratios. Prove an edge-addition monotonicity lemma: if H is obtained from G by adding one missing simple edge, then (-1)^(n-1) det R_H ≤ (-1)^(n-1) det R_G, with strict inequality unless the edge was already present. This should follow from Bapat's determinant expression plus the matrix determinant lemma, or from Loewner monotonicity of reduced Laplacian inverses and the Euclidean-distance-matrix determinant formula. Since every connected simple graph contains a spanning tree and is contained in K_n, the upper bound follows from Graham--Pollak for trees and the lower bound from the explicit resistance matrix of K_n, whose off-diagonal entries are 2/n. Equality cases are forced by strict edge-addition monotonicity.
title: Extremal signed determinant of the resistance matrix of a connected simple graph

description: Conjectures that for all integers $p \ge 3$ and $s \ge 1$, the Cameron-Puleo bound is tight for the graph $K^-_p \cup sK_1$, generalizing the paper's results for $K^-_3 \cup sK_1$ and $K^-_{p-1} \cup K_1$. Specifically, $\mathrm{sat}(n, K_1 \vee (K^-_p \cup sK_1)) = n - 1 + \mathrm{sat}(n-1, K^-_p \cup sK_1)$ for all $n \ge p + s + 1$.
proof_strategy: Induction on $s$, leveraging the structural properties of $K^-_p$-saturated graphs and the edge addition between isolated vertices and the join vertex. The base cases $p=3$ (all $s$) and $s=1$ (all $p \ge 4$) are established in the paper. The inductive step would involve constructing an extremal graph for $s+1$ from the extremal graph for $s$ by carefully adding a new vertex and connecting it to preserve saturation properties, extending the constructive bounds used for $K^-_3 \cup sK_1$.
title: Cameron-Puleo Equality for $K^-_p \cup sK_1$

description: Let A → B be a finite locally free homomorphism of commutative rings of constant rank d. If an invertible A-module P becomes free of rank one after base change to B, then P^{⊗ d} is free; equivalently, the kernel of the pullback map Pic(A) → Pic(B) is annihilated by d. Applied to A = O_K[t]/(f) and B = O_L[t]/(f), this predicts that whenever two non-derogatory integral matrices with characteristic polynomial f become similar over O_L, the associated Latimer--MacDuffee Picard-class difference has order dividing [L : K].
domain_bridges: integral matrix similarity as isomorphism of modules over O_K[t]/(f)
Latimer--MacDuffee correspondence between non-derogatory matrices and ideal/Picard classes of orders
finite locally free norm maps on Picard groups give lower bounds for extension degrees
proof_strategy: Define the norm of an invertible B-module along a finite locally free A-algebra B using determinant of restriction of scalars. Prove the standard identity Norm_{B/A}(B ⊗_A P) ≅ P^{⊗ d} for every invertible A-module P, by localizing on Spec A where P is free rank one and B is free rank d. If B ⊗_A P is trivial in Pic(B), its norm is trivial in Pic(A), hence P^{⊗ d} is trivial. The matrix-similarity consequence follows by transporting similarity to isomorphism of the corresponding rank-one projective modules over the order O_K[t]/(f).
title: Finite-flat capitulation divisibility for Picard classes

description: Conjectures that the upper bound for the Ramsey number $R(T, K_{m_1,\ldots,m_k}) \le (k-1)(R(T, K_{m_1,m_2})-1)+m_1$ established in the resolution of Erdős Problem 550 is tight. Specifically, for any fixed $k \ge 2$ and $1 \le m_1 \le \dots \le m_k$, there exist arbitrarily large trees $T$ for which equality holds, demonstrating that the excess over the canonical Burr lower bound cannot be improved in general.
proof_strategy: Construct a sequence of trees (e.g., specific brooms or generalized stars) that maximize the bipartite excess $R(T, K_{m_1,m_2}) - (|T| + m_1 - 1)$ and prove that these trees simultaneously maximize the multipartite excess against $K_{m_1,\ldots,m_k}$, thereby saturating the upper bound exactly.
title: Tightness of the Erdős 550 Upper Bound for Tree-Multipartite Ramsey Numbers

description: For any prime p and integer i ≥ 1, the codimension-i rational cohomology of the Hecke congruence subgroup Γ_{0,n}(p) vanishes for n ≥ (3i+1)p + (3i+2). Specifically, H^{n(n-1)/2 - i}(Γ_{0,n}(p); ℚ) = 0. This extrapolates the paper's results for i=1 (n ≥ 4p+5) and i=2 (n ≥ 7p+8) to arbitrary codimensions.
proof_strategy: Apply Borel-Serre duality to translate the vanishing of high-degree rational cohomology into the vanishing of low-degree homology of associated complexes of Steinberg modules, then establish high connectivity of complexes of p-modular systems for large n, inductively generalizing the combinatorial topology techniques used for codimensions 1 and 2.
title: Codimension-i Vanishing Conjecture for Hecke Congruence Subgroups

description: For every positive integer h, the set 𝒥_h = {j ≥ 1 : rad(j) = rad(j+h)} is finite with |𝒥_h| ≤ 3 · 7^{3+2ω(h)}, where rad(n) is the product of distinct prime factors of n and ω(h) is the number of distinct prime factors of h. Furthermore, 𝒥_h is empty when h is odd (since rad(j) = rad(j+h) forces 2 | rad(j) = rad(j+h), requiring both j and j+h even, contradicting odd h). This bound, due to Pollack–Pomerance–Treviño, is the crucial finiteness input underpinning the paper's rank-amplified decomposition of S_h^φ(x) into diagonal (Graham–Holt–Pomerance same-support family) and off-diagonal components.
proof_strategy: The proof proceeds in two parts. (1) For odd h: if rad(j) = rad(j+h) and h is odd, then j and j+h have opposite parity, so 2 divides exactly one of rad(j), rad(j+h), a contradiction. Hence 𝒥_h = ∅. (2) For the bound |𝒥_h| ≤ 3·7^{3+2ω(h)}: follow the Pollack–Pomerance–Treviño argument which analyzes the constraint rad(j) = rad(j+h) by factoring out d = gcd(j, j+h) | h, writing j = dm, j+h = d(m+k) where k = h/d, and classifying solutions via the resulting divisibility constraints on prime factors. The bound arises from enumerating prime-signature patterns compatible with rad(m) = rad(m+k), using that each prime factor of h constrains the local options at that prime to finitely many residue classes, with the 7^{2ω(h)} factor accounting for independent choices at each of the ω(h) prime divisors of h.
title: Explicit Finiteness Bound for Same-Radical Shift Sets

description: The authors disprove a conjecture by Cheong, Goaoc, and Holmsen by showing that for every n >= 1, there is a finite family of pairwise disjoint open convex sets in R^{3n} such that the (n-1)-st reduced homology of the space of line transversals is nonzero. They explicitly state the conjecture that this space of line transversals is in fact homotopy equivalent to the (n-1)-sphere, S^{n-1}. This proposes formalizing that stronger homotopy equivalence conjecture.
proof_strategy: Formalize the explicit construction of the disjoint convex sets and the space of line transversals, then construct an explicit homotopy equivalence between the space of line transversals and the (n-1)-dimensional sphere using the topological properties of the constructed space.
title: Homotopy Equivalence of Line Transversal Spaces to Spheres

description: Conjecture that for any prime power $q$ and integer $n \ge q+2$, the Grassmann scheme $J_q(n,2)$ is degree-one trivial (DOT), meaning that all Boolean degree one functions on $J_q(n,2)$ are trivial. This extends Drudge's theorem for $q=3, n \ge 5$ and the known result for $q=2, n \ge 4$, proposing a unified threshold $n \ge q+2$.
proof_strategy: Adapt the eigenvalue bound methods and combinatorial arguments used for small $q$ to the general case. Specifically, show that any non-trivial Boolean degree one function on $J_q(q+2, 2)$ would violate the properties of the association scheme eigenvalues, utilizing the character theory of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ to constrain the coefficients $c_p$ of degree one functions.
title: Degree-One Triviality of Grassmann Schemes $J_q(n,2)$ for $n \ge q+2$

description: The number of binary 2-binomial equivalence classes of words of length n over the alphabet {0,1} equals the n-th cake number, i.e., (n^3 + 5n + 6) / 6 = ∑_{r=0}^{3} C(n,r). This is the identity established by Rigo–Salimov and given geometric explanation in the paper via hyperplane arrangements.
proof_strategy: Define binary 2-binomial equivalence on words via scattered subword counts, then count equivalence classes. The geometric route constructs n hyperplanes in R^3 in general position and establishes a bijection between chambers and equivalence classes; the chamber count follows from the Steiner–Schläfli formula. A direct combinatorial proof would enumerate classes by their defining binomial coefficient invariants.
title: Binary 2-binomial class count equals the cake number

description: For k ≥ 2, let F(k) = gcd_{q=2}^{k} (qk choose k). We conjecture that F(k) = 1 if and only if k is not a prime power. This generalizes the known result for D(k) = gcd_{q=2}^{k+1} (qk choose k) which equals 1 precisely when k+1 is not a prime power (in the sense that the largest prime-power divisor P of k+1 satisfies (k+1)/P > P). The conjecture can be approached using similar techniques: a finite-difference argument shows only primes dividing k can divide F(k), Lucas' theorem reduces the problem to base-p digit analysis, and a digit-box stabilizer theorem determines when F(k) = 1.
proof_strategy: Adapt the proof technique of the original paper: (1) Show that if a prime p divides F(k), then p divides k. (2) For each prime p dividing k, use Lucas' theorem to reduce the question to a digitwise condition in base p. (3) Prove that p divides F(k) if and only if k/p^a ≤ p^a for the largest prime power p^a || k. (4) Conclude that F(k) = 1 iff no such p exists, i.e., k is not a prime power.
title: A Prime-Power Criterion for GCDs of Binomial Coefficients with Restricted Upper Index Range

description: Conjecture: For any finite group Γ, any real-valued function f : Γ → ℝ, and any finite directed graph F, the homomorphism density t(F, C_f) satisfies t(F, C_f) ≥ (E_Gamma f)^(2 * e(F)), and equality holds iff f is constant on Γ.
proof_strategy: Apply repeated Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities on the group sum to bound the kernel average, and argue that equality forces f to be constant.
title: Conjecture on extremal constantness for two-sided group correlation kernels

description: This conjecture proposes a universal structural condition that determines whether the deleted co-maximal subgroup graph of a finite group is connected, and when it has cycles or becomes a star.
proof_strategy: Constructive analysis combining subgroup inclusion properties with graph connectivity criteria
title: Connectivity of co-maximal subgroup graphs for finite groups

description: For any graph G, the externally supported independence number α_{es}(G) is at least α(G) - 1, where α(G) is the standard independence number of G. This conjecture posits that the additional ES-condition does not reduce the maximum independent set size by more than one, even in cases where the standard independence number is achievable without the ES-condition.
proof_strategy: Prove the bound α_{es}(G) ≥ α(G) - 1 holds universally by constructing an ESI-set from an arbitrary maximum independent set through local modifications to satisfy the ES-condition, or disprove by finding a graph where the reduction exceeds 1.
title: Lower Bound Conjecture for Externally Supported Independence Number

description: An infinite word $x_1x_2\dots \in \mathcal{A}^\mathbb{N}$ is realized as the $\beta$-expansion $d(x,\beta)$ for some real number $x \in [0, 1)$ if and only if for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the tail $x_nx_{n+1}\dots$ is lexicographically strictly less than the quasi-greedy $\beta$-expansion of 1, $d^*(1,\beta)$.
proof_strategy: Define the lexicographic order on infinite sequences over a finite alphabet, formalize the $\beta$-transformation and the quasi-greedy expansion of 1, then prove the equivalence using properties of the shift map and greedy expansions.
title: Parry's Theorem on Admissible Beta-Expansions

description: For any prime $p$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, let $P_3$ denote the 3-dimensional paraboloid over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$. The endpoint restriction conjecture for $P_3$ states that the Fourier extension operator associated with $P_3$ maps $L^2(P_3)$ to $L^3(\mathbb{F}_p^3)$ with a constant independent of $p$. Equivalently, for any function $f: P_3 \to \mathbb{C}$, $\| E(f) \|_{L^3(\mathbb{F}_p^3)} \le C \|f\|_{L^2(P_3)}$ where $E(f)(x) = p^{-2} \sum_{\xi \in P_3} f(\xi) e(x \cdot \xi)$ and $C$ is an absolute constant.
proof_strategy: Extend the author's bilinear approach and point-line incidence estimates to handle the endpoint $r=3$, or establish sharp Kakeya and maximal restriction bounds over finite fields to close the remaining gap.
title: Finite Field Restriction Conjecture for the 3D Paraboloid

description: Conjecture: Let r,t,n be natural numbers with 1 ≤ t ≤ r and n ≥ r+1. Let K be a pure r-dimensional simplicial complex on n vertices which is r-down path connected. Suppose that for every face σ of K with |σ| = r - t, the reduced homology group H_t(lk_K(σ); ℝ) vanishes. Then q_{r-1}(K) = t n - (t-1)(r+1) if and only if K is isomorphic to Δ_{r+1-t} ⋆ Δ_{n-r-1+t}^{t}. Equivalently, the large lower bound on n appearing in the paper’s equality characterization is unnecessary.
domain_bridges: local link homology constraints ↔ extremal spectral radius
pure simplicial complexes ↔ uniform hypergraphs with downward closure
r-down path connectivity ↔ irreducibility of the signless up-Laplacian
join of a simplex with a skeleton ↔ extremal Perron-equality structure
proof_strategy: Formalize the paper’s inequality proof via the Rayleigh quotient for the nonnegative signless up-Laplacian. Use r-down path connectivity to obtain irreducibility and hence a strictly positive Perron vector. Analyze every equality condition in the chain of inequalities: local homology vanishing should force the relevant link shadows to attain their extremal Kruskal-Katona-type lower bounds, while equality in the Perron/Rayleigh estimates should force all maximal r-faces to contain a common core of size r+1-t and to contain every t-subset of the complementary vertex set. The remaining task is to replace the paper’s large-n rigidity lemma by an exact finite rigidity lemma for the equality case.
title: Threshold-free equality case for the local-homology signless Laplacian bound

description: The lazy swap chain on the set Ω(r,c) of m×n binary matrices with prescribed row sums r and column sums c has spectral gap at least (C(m,2))⁻¹(C(n,2))⁻¹ for all feasible margins whenever m,n ≥ 2. This resolves the 1997 conjecture of Kannan, Tetali, and Vempala. The bound is tight in the worst case (e.g., r₁=r₂=1, c₁=c₂=1, all other margins zero, giving |Ω|=2).
proof_strategy: Follow the paper's three-stage argument: (1) Establish a comparison inequality between the swap chain and a two-row heat-bath chain, bounding the swap chain spectral gap from below by a constant times the heat-bath spectral gap. (2) Reduce the m×n heat-bath analysis to the 3-row case via a tensorization/reduction argument on the column-count variable. (3) Prove the 3-row inequality by decomposing the function space on {0,1}³ into the constant sector, the count sector (functions of the column sum), and the Johnson harmonic sectors, establishing a Poincaré inequality on each sector with the appropriate spectral gap lower bound.
title: Spectral Gap Lower Bound for the Binary Fixed-Margin Swap Chain

description: For every nonempty m × n rectangular grid, let f : {0,…,m−1} × {0,…,n−1} → Z satisfy f(0,0)=0 and |f(p)-f(q)|≤1 on every grid edge. Then the total absolute mass is at most n·m(m−1)/2 + m·n(n−1)/2. This bound is sharp, attained by f(i,j)=i+j and by f(i,j)=−(i+j). In the Miura-ori height-function model this is exactly the extremal inequality needed to turn the explicit lower-bound construction for the flip-graph diameter into a matching upper bound whenever flip distance is controlled by L1 height difference.
domain_bridges: Miura-ori flip graphs reduce to recolouring graphs of proper 3-colourings of rectangular grid graphs.
Proper 3-colourings lift to integer height functions with adjacent differences ±1.
Differences of two normalized height functions are integer-valued 1-Lipschitz grid functions, so flip-graph diameter bounds reduce to an L1 extremal inequality.
proof_strategy: Prove pointwise that any edge-1-Lipschitz f with f(0,0)=0 satisfies |f(i,j)| ≤ i+j by following a shortest Manhattan path from (0,0) to (i,j). Sum this pointwise bound over all grid vertices. Evaluate the two separable sums ∑_{i=0}^{m−1}∑_{j=0}^{n−1}(i+j)=n·m(m−1)/2 + m·n(n−1)/2. Sharpness follows by checking that f(i,j)=i+j is edge-1-Lipschitz, normalized at the origin, and attains equality termwise.
title: Extremal L1 mass of normalized 1-Lipschitz grid height differences

description: Conjecture: For any finite simple graph G, the number of irreducible FAT colorings of G is exactly the cardinality of the set of real numbers α ∈ [0,1] for which there exists β ∈ [0,1] such that (α,β) yields a FAT coloring of G. In other words, each irreducible FAT coloring corresponds to a unique fairness parameter α, and distinct irreducible FAT colorings give distinct α values.
proof_strategy: Show that merging color classes in a FAT coloring scales the fairness parameter α by a predictable rational factor (as described in the paper). Hence, along any chain in the coarsening poset, the α values form a strictly decreasing sequence. Irreducible FAT colorings are precisely the minimal elements in this poset, so each yields a distinct α that cannot be obtained by scaling another α. Conversely, given any α arising from a FAT coloring, repeatedly refine the coloring while preserving the FAT property until an irreducible coloring is reached; this process does not change α. This establishes a bijection between irreducible FAT colorings and distinct α values.
title: Number of irreducible FAT colorings equals number of distinct fairness parameters

description: Every 3-connected planar graph with an even number of vertices has at least 3 perfect matchings. While the paper establishes that the minimum non-zero number of perfect matchings for 3-connected planar graphs is bounded by a constant, this conjecture posits that the exact constant is 3, which is achieved by the complete graph on 4 vertices.
proof_strategy: Use Tutte's theorem and structural properties of 3-connected planar graphs to show that such a graph cannot have exactly 1 or 2 perfect matchings. A graph with exactly 2 perfect matchings must have a Hamiltonian cycle as its symmetric difference, which imposes restrictive structural constraints incompatible with 3-connectivity in planar graphs.
title: Exact Minimum Perfect Matchings in 3-Connected Planar Graphs

description: For every primitive integer 2 by 2 matrix M with nonzero determinant, the values k(Mx) / k(x) obtained by restricting x to real quadratic irrational badly approximable numbers are dense in the full interval [1 / |det M|, |det M|]. Equivalently, for every real u < v with 1 / |det M| <= u < v <= |det M|, there exists a real quadratic irrational x such that u < k(Mx) / k(x) < v.
domain_bridges: continued fractions to real quadratic irrationals via eventual periodicity
