proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's construction realizing arbitrary ratios in the interval by bounded continued fraction sequences, but replace the infinite nonperiodic tail by sufficiently long periodic repetitions of the finite blocks controlling the limsup. Since ultimately periodic continued fractions are quadratic irrationals, it remains to prove that the Lagrange-constant ratio changes by an arbitrarily small amount under this periodic approximation. Formalization would isolate a continuity lemma for finite-window limsup maxima of periodic continued fractions and combine it with the Smith-normal-form reduction used for the general matrix M.
title: Quadratic irrational density in the ratio spectrum

description: The sum of the elements in the $n$-th row of the Pascal-like Riordan array defined by the power series pair $(1/(1-x), x/(1-x)^2)$, whose entries are given by the binomial coefficient $t_{n,k} = \binom{n+k}{2k}$, equals the $(2n+1)$-th Fibonacci number. This is derived from the paper's demonstration that the generating function of the row sums is $(1-x)/(1-3x+x^2)$, which characterizes the odd-indexed Fibonacci sequence.
proof_strategy: 1. Define the lower-triangular matrix $T$ with entries $T_{n,k} = \binom{n+k}{2k}$ for $0 \le k \le n$. 2. Show that the row sums $S_n = \sum_{k=0}^n T_{n,k}$ correspond to the coefficients of the generating function $\frac{1-x}{1-3x+x^2}$. 3. Prove that the sequence generated by $\frac{1-x}{1-3x+x^2}$ satisfies the Fibonacci recurrence $S_n = 3S_{n-1} - S_{n-2}$ with initial conditions $S_0 = 1, S_1 = 2$. 4. Prove by induction that $S_n = F_{2n+1}$, where $F_m$ is the $m$-th Fibonacci number.
title: Row Sum Fibonacci Property of Pascal-like Riordan Array

description: Every Hamiltonian connected cubic edge-transitive graph Γ has Hamiltonian compression factor κ(Γ) ≥ 2, i.e., it admits a 2-symmetric Hamiltonian cycle: there exists a Hamiltonian cycle C and an automorphism g of order 2 such that g acts on C as a rotation by |V(Γ)|/2 positions. This is supported by exhaustive computation on all such graphs up to 10,000 vertices, where every Hamiltonian cubic edge-transitive graph was found to have κ ≥ 2.
proof_strategy: Leverage the edge-transitivity of Γ to show that any Hamiltonian cycle can be 'symmetrized': given a Hamiltonian cycle C, use the transitivity of Aut(Γ) on edges of Γ to construct an involutory automorphism that permutes the edges of C as a half-rotation. The key step is showing that edge-transitivity forces enough symmetry on the edge set of any Hamiltonian cycle to guarantee a 2-fold rotational symmetry. Alternatively, classify cubic edge-transitive graphs by their automorphism group structure and verify case-by-case for each infinite family (e.g., generalized Petersen graphs, Möbius ladders, prism graphs).
title: Hamiltonian Compression Factor of Cubic Edge-Transitive Graphs

description: In Lemma 2.1 of the paper the infinite right half-strip row-exchange identity is proved under a uniform contraction assumption for every column. Conjecture: the same identity remains valid under the strictly weaker hypothesis that the contraction ratio is eventually bounded by some δ < 1. More precisely, for arbitrary top and bottom boundary occupation sequences, nonzero α, and spectral parameters v,z, if there exist δ < 1 and N such that for all i ≥ N the norm of (w₁(uᵢ/z)/w₄(uᵢ/z))*(w₄(uᵢ/v)/w₁(uᵢ/v)) is at most δ, then the two infinite row-exchange partition functions are equal up to the same scalar prefactor f(v/z)/α².
domain_bridges: Yang-Baxter row commutation as an equality of finite transfer-matrix partition sums
Infinite-volume partition functions as limits of finite truncations
Geometric tail bounds formalized using normed-field estimates and Tendsto
proof_strategy: Define finite truncations of the two row-exchange diagrams at column n. The finite Yang-Baxter equation gives exact equality except for a boundary term where the unique path exits through the artificial right boundary. Show that this boundary term is bounded by C times the product of the contraction ratios from N to n. The eventual δ-bound gives a geometric estimate C*δ^(n-N), hence the boundary term tends to zero. Taking limits of the finite identities yields the infinite row-exchange identity for arbitrary boundary occupation sequences.
title: Row-exchange under eventual contraction for the infinite asymmetric five-vertex half-strip

description: For every integer t ≥ 1 and q ≥ 1, let F = tK₂ ∪ qK₁ be the disjoint union of a matching of size t and q isolated vertices. Then for every n > 2t + q, the Cameron--Puleo upper bound is tight: sat(n, K₁ ∨ F) = n - 1 + sat(n - 1, F). This extends the paper's proved cases t = 1 and t = 2 to all matchings with isolated vertices.
domain_bridges: finite simple graph theory to Lean 4 SimpleGraph
extremal combinatorics to finite cardinal minimization
graph joins and disjoint unions to type-level finite graph constructions
proof_strategy: The upper bound is exactly the Cameron--Puleo construction: take an extremal F-saturated graph on n-1 vertices and join one new universal vertex to it. For the lower bound, let G be any (K1∨F)-saturated graph on n vertices. Analyze a nonedge xy and the forced copy of K1∨F in G+xy. Because F is a matching plus isolated vertices, any forced copy can be decomposed into one apex vertex, t independent edges, and q remaining vertices avoiding the apex constraints. Show that the saturation condition forces either a universal vertex whose deletion is F-saturated, giving |E(G)| ≥ n-1+sat(n-1,F), or else enough local edge-disjoint matching witnesses around nonedges to yield the same global edge lower bound by degree counting. The base cases t=1,2 are supplied by the paper; the induction step increases t by removing one forced matching edge from each witness copy and applying the lower bound to the residual (t-1)K2∪qK1 configuration.
title: Join-saturation equality for matchings with isolated vertices

description: For any integer k >= 3, the sum of 2^{k_2} * zeta(k_1, k_2) over all positive integers k_1, k_2 such that k_1 + k_2 = k and k_2 >= 2, equals (k + 1) * zeta(k). This theorem is explicitly mentioned in the paper as the foundational starting point that is generalized to multiple mixed values.
proof_strategy: Apply generating functions and the stuffle product relations of multiple zeta values, or adapt the iterated integral representation approach introduced in the paper for multiple mixed values.
title: Ohno-Zudilin Weighted Sum Formula for Double Zeta Values

description: Let 𝔓(y)=Σ_{a∈A} c_a(t) Π_{i=0}^k (y^(i))^{a_i} be a nonzero ordinary algebraic differential polynomial over algebraically closed characteristic-zero Hahn series with finite support A. Let E_k(trop(𝔓)) be the set of t-adic orders r of Boolean Hahn elementary k-solutions of its tropicalization, equivalently the r for which the active indicial tropical minimum is attained at least twice. For each r in E_k(trop(𝔓)), form the classical indicial initial polynomial I_r(Z) in the leading coefficient Z, using exactly the monomials attaining that minimum and the falling-factorial factors coming from derivatives. Conjecture: if every r in E_k(trop(𝔓)) has a simple nonzero root of I_r(Z), then every elementary tropical order is realized by an actual Hahn-series solution; hence ord_t(Sol(𝔓)) = E_k(trop(𝔓)). This strengthens the paper's containment ord_t(Sol(𝔓)) ⊆ E_k(trop(𝔓)) to equality under a Newton-nondegeneracy hypothesis.
domain_bridges: Boolean tropical differential equations ↔ valuations of Hahn-series differential equations
indicial tropical corner locus ↔ leading-term cancellation in algebraic ODEs
simple initial root ↔ Newton-Hensel lifting for formal differential equations
proof_strategy: Prove the known tropicalization inclusion first: the order of any Hahn solution forces at least two lowest-valued differential monomials, so it lies in E_k(trop(𝔓)). For the reverse inclusion, fix r in E_k and choose a simple nonzero root c of the indicial polynomial I_r. Substitute y = c t^r + z with ord(z) > r. Develop a transfinite Newton-Hensel recursion on the well-ordered support of z. At each stage, the simple-root condition makes the linearized initial operator invertible for the next coefficient, preventing resonant obstructions. Show that the constructed support remains well ordered, so the recursion defines a Hahn series y satisfying 𝔓(y)=0 and ord_t(y)=r. Formalization would isolate the differential-polynomial combinatorics, falling-factorial leading terms, and a Hahn-series transfinite recursion lemma.
title: Newton-nondegenerate elementary tropical orders lift to Hahn-series solutions

description: Let d >= 4 and let K = Q(sqrt((d+1)(d-3))) be real quadratic with maximal order O_K. For an integer f > 0 with gcd(d,f)=1, let K^{fd} be the ordinary ray class field of K of finite modulus fd attached to O_K, and let K_L^{d;f} be the Kopp--Lagarias ray class field of finite modulus d attached to the order Z + f O_K. Define the canonical totally positive unit u = (d - 1 + sqrt((d+1)(d-3)))/2. Let P_f = (O_K/f O_K)^× / (Z/fZ)^×, and let [u]_f be the image of u in P_f. The conjecture is that the excess e(d,f) = [K^{fd} : K_L^{d;f}] equals the index of the cyclic subgroup generated by [u]_f in P_f. Equivalently, e(d,f) = |P_f| / order([u]_f), and when f is prime to the discriminant this is Phi_K(f)/(Phi(f) * order([u]_f)). This gives a precise class-field-theoretic explanation for when the non-maximal ray class field is a proper subfield of the maximal ray class field.

proof_strategy: Use the exact sequence comparing the ray class group of the maximal order modulo fd with the ray class group of the non-maximal order Z + f O_K modulo d. Under the coprimality hypothesis gcd(d,f)=1, the kernel should be identified via Artin reciprocity with the projective residue-unit group (O_K/fO_K)^×/(Z/fZ)^×, modulo the subgroup generated by the reduction of the totally positive SIC unit u. The degree ratio of the corresponding class fields is therefore the index of <[u]_f>. A Lean formalization would first define the two ray class groups as quotients of fractional ideals prime to the relevant modulus, prove the comparison exact sequence, then translate subgroup index into extension degree using finite Galois correspondence.
title: Excess of Kopp--Lagarias ray class fields is the projective order defect of the SIC unit

description: The paper proves R(T, K_{m₁,…,mₖ}) ≤ (k−1)(R(T, K_{m₁,m₂}) − 1) + m₁ for all sufficiently large n-vertex trees T. We conjecture this bound holds for ALL trees T with |T| ≥ mₖ, removing the asymptotic 'sufficiently large n' condition. This would extend the resolution of Erdős Problem 550 to a universal statement and subsumes Chvátal's theorem R(T, Kₖ) = (k−1)(|T|−1)+1 as the special case m₁=⋯=mₖ=1. Verified for n=1,2 and the paper's asymptotic regime; the intermediate range requires new techniques.
proof_strategy: The paper's proof invokes Szemerédi regularity which forces n to be enormous. Removing the asymptotic condition requires replacing regularity-based embedding with direct structural arguments for small and medium n. The approach would proceed in three stages: (1) verify the bound for small trees via exhaustive analysis of extremal colorings near the Turán threshold, (2) develop a regularity-free off-Turán embedding for medium-sized trees using the Hladký–Piguet local matching lemma directly on structured colorings, and (3) apply the paper's compactness rounding for large n. The base case reduces to Chvátal's theorem when all mᵢ=1.
title: Universal Erdős 550: Tree–Multipartite Ramsey Bound Without Asymptotic Conditions

description: For fixed integers k ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ m₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ mₖ, there exists n₀ = n₀(m₁,…,mₖ) such that for every n ≥ n₀ and every n-vertex tree T, R(T, K_{m₁,…,mₖ}) ≤ (k−1)(R(T, K_{m₁,m₂}) − 1) + m₁. This resolves Erdős Problem 550 and establishes that the excess over the Burr canonical lower bound is controlled by the excess in the bipartite subproblem involving the two smallest parts.
proof_strategy: Formalize in stages: (1) Burr's canonical lower bound R(T,F) ≥ (χ(F)−1)(|T|−1)+σ(F) and Chvátal's theorem R(T,K_k)=(k−1)(|T|−1)+1 as base cases. (2) Formalize Szemerédi's regularity lemma and the local regular-matching embedding lemma of Hladký–Piguet. (3) Prove the off-Turán tree-embedding theorem: in any sufficiently dense graph relative to the Turán density, a large tree can be embedded. (4) Formalize the compactness-and-rounding theorem for represented bounded-rank hypergraph obstructions using shadow hypergraphs. (5) Combine to derive the Ramsey capacity contradiction that yields the main inequality.
title: Erdős Problem 550: Tree versus Complete Multipartite Ramsey Upper Bound

description: For any left-regular bipartite graph G of degree d ≥ 3 with girth at least 2s (equivalently, G is s-optimal), the binary linear code B(G) has minimum distance at least 2(d-1)^{s-2}. This conjecture asserts that the girth characterization of s-optimal expanders proven in the paper transfers to a strong lower bound on the minimum distance of the associated code, providing the coding-theoretic foundation needed for the post-quantum key exchange application.
proof_strategy: Use the girth ≥ 2s condition to show that any nonempty subset X ⊆ L with |X| < 2(d-1)^{s-2} cannot have all right vertices with even-degree neighborhoods (the parity condition defining B(G)), by arguing that the local tree structure around small sets forces at least one right vertex to have odd degree in the induced subgraph. The factor of 2 arises from the bipartite structure and the even-girth constraint.
title: Girth-Implied Minimum Distance Bound for Optimal Small-Set Expander Codes

catalog_references: Fomin-Zelevinsky finite type classification of cluster algebras
description: For the standard rectangular/plabic cluster seed on the coordinate ring of the Grassmannian partial flag variety Gr(k,n), the cluster algebra is of finite type exactly in the classical finite Grassmannian cases: k=1 or n-k=1, k=2 or n-k=2, or (min(k,n-k),n) equal to (3,6), (3,7), or (3,8). Moreover the Dynkin type is respectively A0, A_{n-3}, D4, E6, and E8; in all other cases the seed is not mutation-equivalent to any Dynkin quiver.
domain_bridges: partial flag coordinate rings to combinatorial quiver mutation
Grassmannian Plucker seeds to rectangular grid quivers
finite cluster type to Dynkin Cartan companions
quiver mutation equivalence to finite ADE classification
proof_strategy: Formalize the rectangular Grassmannian seed as a finite quiver with frozen boundary vertices. Define mutation equivalence and finite cluster type using Fomin-Zelevinsky's criterion: a skew-symmetrizable exchange matrix is of finite type iff some matrix in its mutation class has Cartan counterpart a finite Dynkin Cartan matrix. Prove by explicit mutation sequences that the listed finite cases reduce to Dynkin quivers A_{n-3}, D4, E6, or E8. For the remaining cases, exhibit a mutation-invariant obstruction or a mutable full subquiver whose Cartan companion is affine/indefinite, proving non-finite type.
title: Finite-type classification for Grassmannian partial-flag seeds

description: The only natural numbers n for which n!/8 is a triangular number are n = 4, 5, and 7; equivalently, the only Brown numbers satisfying n! + 1 = m^2 are (4,5), (5,11), and (7,71). This is falsifiable by exhibiting any n ≥ 8 and integer y with y*(y+1)/2 = n!/8, or equivalently any m with n! + 1 = m^2.
proof_strategy: Formalize the triangular equivalence lemma: for n ≥ 4, n! + 1 = m^2 iff there exists y such that y*(y+1)/2 = n!/8 and m = 2*y + 1. Then attempt to prove the classification by combining modular exclusions for residue classes of n with factorial divisibility facts and higher-power congruence obstructions. The conjecture is suitable for Lean because it can be stated entirely over Nat using factorials, squares, divisibility by 8, and triangular numbers.
title: Brocard-Ramanujan Triangular Classification

description: The paper establishes that for almost all n, g_k(n) ≥ (3(k-1)/log 12 − ε) log n, while pointwise g_k(n) ≤ (k-1)/log 2 · log n + O(log log n). The gap between 3/log 12 ≈ 1.207 and 1/log 2 ≈ 1.443 motivates the conjecture that the upper bound coefficient is asymptotically tight: for every k ≥ 2 and ε > 0, the set of n ≤ x with g_k(n) < ((k−1)/log 2 − ε) log n has cardinality o(x). This would mean binary carries are the essential obstruction and c_k = (k−1)/log 2 is the true almost-everywhere constant, resolving Erdős Problem 400.
proof_strategy: Establish that the binary carry obstruction is not just an upper bound but the typical behavior. Likely requires: (1) strengthening the S-unit digit-sum normal-order theorem from the paper to handle all prime bases simultaneously rather than just base 2 and 3; (2) showing that the mixed-base 2-3 construction achieving 3/log 12 can be bootstrapped toward 1/log 2 by incorporating larger prime factors via the Kummer sieve uniformly; (3) developing quantitative multi-block estimates for carry patterns across all primes p ≤ n, showing that the typical n achieves near-maximal carry contributions. An ergodic-theoretic approach via equidistribution on S-unit progressions may yield the necessary uniformity.
title: Tight Almost-Everywhere Coefficient for Erdős Excess Function g_k

description: For every n ≥ 1, let I_n be the explicit finite family of pairwise disjoint bounded open convex subsets of R^(3n) obtained by the inflation step in the paper's proof of Theorem t:inflated_intro. Then the full space of unoriented line transversals to I_n, with the standard affine-Grassmannian topology, is homotopy equivalent to S^(n-1). This strengthens the paper's nonvanishing reduced homology conclusion to a complete homotopy-type identification for the constructed examples.
domain_bridges: convex geometry of line transversals -> affine Grassmannian topology
explicit geometric construction -> definable finite family in EuclideanSpace R (Fin (3*n))
homology nonvanishing -> homotopy equivalence with a sphere
geometric deformation retraction -> Lean formalization using ContinuousMap/Homotopy
proof_strategy: Formalize the paper's inflated family I_n explicitly. Parametrize a line transversal by the same block-coordinate data used in the construction. Define a continuous map from the transversal space to the unit sphere in R^n extracting the normalized parameter vector, and define a section from S^(n-1) by choosing the canonical transversal line associated to each parameter. Prove that the two composites are homotopic to the identities, using convexity of the inflated sets to keep the interpolated lines transversal throughout the homotopy. The key Lean tasks are: define the topology on unoriented affine lines, prove openness/convexity/disjointness of I_n, prove continuity of the parameter maps, and formalize the deformation homotopies.
title: Inflated line-transversal counterexamples have sphere homotopy type

catalog_references: Arocha--Bracho--Montejano Helly theorem for convex splinters: Helly number 2d+1
Alon--Kleitman proof of the Hadwiger--Debrunner (p,q) theorem
description: For every dimension d and integers p >= q >= 2d+1, there is a constant N = N(d,p,q) such that any finite family F of convex splinters in R^d with the (p,q)-property admits a transversal of size at most N. Here the (p,q)-property means that among every p members of F, some q members have nonempty common intersection. This extends the classical Hadwiger--Debrunner theorem from convex sets to convex splinters, with the Helly threshold 2d+1 replacing d+1.
domain_bridges: combinatorial geometry ↔ Lean finite family formalization
proof_strategy: Formalize convex splinters as finite unions of convex sets satisfying the minimal affine-dependence containment axiom. Combine the paper's fractional Helly theorem for convex splinters with the standard Alon--Kleitman bootstrapping scheme: derive a weak epsilon-net or selection lemma appropriate to splinters, then use the (p,q)-property to obtain a bounded-size hitting set. The Lean development can separate the abstract finite-set-system part from the geometric input, so that the final theorem only requires the convex-splinter fractional Helly lemma and the Helly number 2d+1.
title: Hadwiger--Debrunner (p,q) theorem for convex splinters

description: In the Wall-Menger theorem (Theorem 1 of the paper), for positive integers s' and t', there exist t and f such that given a vertex set A and a wall W of size at least t, either (i) a vertex set X of size at most f separates A from the branch vertices of W, or (ii) a subwall W' of size at least t' admits s' disjoint A-W' paths each ending in a distinct nail of W'. The conjecture asserts that the optimal bound on the separator size is f(s') = s' - 1, matching the classical Menger theorem exactly, regardless of the wall structure.
proof_strategy: Formalize walls, branch vertices, nails, subwalls, and A-W paths in Lean. Prove the lower bound f >= s'-1 by constructing a graph where any separator must have size s'-1 (e.g., a wall with s'-1 vertices on a single subdivided edge acting as a bottleneck). For the upper bound, attempt to show that if no set of s'-1 vertices separates A from the branch vertices of W, then by iterated application of Menger's theorem and the grid structure of walls, one can route s' disjoint paths to distinct nails of a suitably large subwall, possibly after discarding a bounded portion of W.
title: Optimal separator bound in the Wall-Menger theorem matches Menger's theorem

description: The codimension-i rational cohomology of the special linear group SL_n(Z) vanishes for n >= i+2. Equivalently, the i-th rational cohomology group H^i(SL_n(Z); Q) is trivial for all i >= (n choose 2) - n + 2.
proof_strategy: Construct a highly connected complex of unimodular vectors or forests over the integers, and use it to establish the vanishing of the rational homology in high degrees, extending the combinatorial and homological methods used for i=0, 1, and 2.
title: Church-Farb-Putman Vanishing Conjecture for SL_n(Z)

description: For every positive integer j and every odd positive integer h, the prime radicals of j and j+h are unequal. Equivalently, the same-prime-support index set J_h = {j ≥ 1 : rad(j) = rad(j+h)} is empty whenever h is odd. This formalizes the elementary obstruction behind the paper's statement that the Graham--Holt--Pomerance diagonal contribution is empty for odd shifts.
domain_bridges: analytic shifted-totient counting to finite radical-support obstruction
GHP diagonal parametrization to parity of prime supports
Euler totient equality problem to elementary divisibility
proof_strategy: Define rad n as the product of all primes dividing n, or equivalently use the predicate that two integers have the same prime divisors. If rad(j) = rad(j+h), then 2 divides j iff 2 divides j+h. But when h is odd, j and j+h have opposite parity, so exactly one of them is divisible by 2. Hence their radicals cannot be equal. In Lean, this can be proved by rewriting oddness as h % 2 = 1 and using parity of addition modulo 2.
title: Odd shifts have no same-support GHP diagonal

description: Conjecture: for d = 3 and n = 8, the maximum size of a 4-uniform family on an 8-element ground set with VC-dimension at most 3 is exactly 40. Equivalently, M_3(8) = 40, which is one larger than the Ahlswede--Khachatrian value binom(7,3)+binom(4,1)=39. This is a finite, fully checkable strengthening of the paper's phenomenon at the smallest admissible ground-set size n=2d+2.
domain_bridges: Encode a 4-uniform set family as a Finset of Finset (Fin 8).
Express VC-dimension at most 3 by forbidding any 4-subset whose trace set is the full powerset.
Reduce the upper bound M_3(8) ≤ 40 to a finite Boolean unsatisfiability certificate over the 70 possible 4-edges.
Prove the lower bound by giving an explicit 40-edge certificate and checking non-shattering in Lean.
proof_strategy: Formalize the finite extremal problem directly. For the lower bound, provide a concrete Finset of 40 four-subsets of Fin 8 and verify that no 4-subset is shattered. For the upper bound, use symmetry under permutations of Fin 8 to reduce cases, then generate a SAT/DRAT or custom branch-and-bound certificate showing that every 41-edge subfamily shatters some 4-subset. The Lean proof should only trust a small checker for the certificate plus elementary finset/cardinality lemmas.
title: Exact first 4-uniform VC extremal value beyond Ahlswede--Khachatrian

description: For every integer t ≥ 1, the asymptotic density c_t of nonnegative integers n such that s₂(n+t) ≥ s₂(n) satisfies c_t ≥ 1/2 + 2^(-(2·s₂(t)+1)), where s₂(m) denotes the number of ones in the binary expansion of m. This is the main theorem proved in the paper, resolving Cusick's conjecture with an explicit quantitative gap.
proof_strategy: The proof decomposes into four major steps amenable to separate formalization: (1) Establish the existence of the density c_t via the exact deconvolution identity that replaces the distribution of s₂(n+t)-s₂(n) with a finite stopped random-walk law over the carry blocks of t. (2) Formalize the principal subsequence ideal structure that indexes the carry block decomposition. (3) Prove the first-exit median comparison lemma for the stopped random walk, showing the median of the exit distribution is nonnegatively biased. (4) Combine the deconvolution with the median bound to derive c_t ≥ 1/2 + 2^(-(2s₂(t)+1)). Steps (1)-(2) are combinatorial and involve 2-adic carry arithmetic; step (3) is probabilistic and requires stochastic ordering arguments.
title: Cusick's Sum-of-Digits Explicit Bound

description: Let G be a simple graph on n vertices with m edges, and define N(S_{2,1},G)=∑_v d(v)(d(v)-1)(n-1-d(v)). If 8m ≤ n(n-1), then N(S_{2,1},G) is maximized by the quasi-clique Q(n,m): writing m = binom(q,2)+r with 0 ≤ r < q, Q(n,m) consists of a K_q, one additional vertex adjacent to exactly r vertices of the clique, and all remaining vertices isolated. Equivalently, the asymptotic low-density upper branch proved in the paper admits an exact finite-n strengthening throughout the range β ≤ 1/4.
domain_bridges: finite strengthening of graphon/asymptotic extremal profiles
proof_strategy: Formalize N(S_{2,1},G) as a degree-sum functional. Prove that any maximizer in the range 8m ≤ n(n-1) can be transformed, via edge-compressions preserving the number of edges, into a threshold graph without decreasing the functional. Then classify threshold graphs in this sparse range and show that every non-quasi-clique threshold configuration admits a local edge transfer increasing or preserving N until the quasi-clique degree sequence is reached. The final step is a finite arithmetic verification using m = binom(q,2)+r.
title: Finite low-density quasi-clique extremality for the semi-induced star S_{2,1}

catalog_references: Erdos--Ko--Rado theorem for intersecting uniform families
Hilton--Milner theorem for non-trivial intersecting families
Pyber product theorem for two cross-intersecting families
Frankl--Wang non-trivial cross-intersection product conjecture proved in the paper
description: For every n,k,r with n ≥ 2k, k ≥ 3, and r ≥ 2, let (𝓕_i)_{i∈Fin r} be k-uniform families of subsets of Fin n. Assume each 𝓕_i is non-trivial, meaning it is not contained in any star, and assume the families are pairwise cross-intersecting: for i ≠ j, every A ∈ 𝓕_i and B ∈ 𝓕_j have A ∩ B ≠ ∅. Then the multilateral product is bounded by the Hilton--Milner value: ∏_{i∈Fin r} |𝓕_i| ≤ h(n,k)^r, where h(n,k) = C(n-1,k-1) - C(n-k-1,k-1) + 1.
domain_bridges: Represents k-uniform set families as Finset (Finset (Fin n)) in Lean 4.
Reduces an r-family product inequality to the two-family sharp product theorem by multiplying pairwise inequalities over unordered pairs.
Connects extremal set theory with finite products and binomial coefficient arithmetic in Nat.
proof_strategy: Formalize the paper's two-family theorem as a Lean lemma: for any two non-star k-uniform cross-intersecting families A,B ⊆ binom(Fin n,k), |A|*|B| ≤ h(n,k)^2. Apply this lemma to every unordered pair of distinct indices i,j ∈ Fin r. Multiplying all pairwise inequalities gives (∏ᵢ |𝓕_i|)^(r-1) ≤ (h(n,k)^r)^(r-1), since each |𝓕_i| occurs in exactly r-1 pair products. Use positivity/monotonicity of natural powers to extract the (r-1)-st root, noting r ≥ 2.
title: Multilateral non-trivial cross-intersection product bound

description: For q ≥ 3 and n ≥ 4, there exists a non-trivial Boolean degree one function on the Grassmann scheme J_q(n,2) that is not in the trivial list (0, 1, x_p, 1-x_p, y_r, 1-y_r, x_p+y_r, 1-x_p-y_r).
proof_strategy: Construct a specific Boolean degree one function using a quadratic form (e.g., a conic or quadric) that violates triviality conditions, inspired by the q=3, n=4, k=2 example.
title: Existence of Non-Trivial Boolean Degree One Functions on J_q(n,2) for q ≥ 3 and n ≥ 4

description: For fixed integers $k \ge 2$ and $1 \le m_1 \le \cdots \le m_k$, there exists an integer $n_0$ such that for all $n \ge n_0$ and every $n$-vertex tree $T$, the Ramsey number satisfies $R(T, K_{m_1, \ldots, m_k}) \le (k-1)(R(T, K_{m_1, m_2})-1)+m_1$.
proof_strategy: Establish an off-Turán tree-embedding theorem via Szemerédi regularity and a local regular-matching lemma, then derive a contradiction by applying a compactness-and-rounding theorem for represented bounded-rank hypergraph obstructions using shadow hypergraphs.
title: Resolution of Erdős Problem 550 on Tree versus Complete Multipartite Ramsey Numbers

description: Conjecture: Let G be a finite left-regular bipartite graph of left degree d ≥ 2 with left vertex set L and right vertex set R. Suppose G is s-optimal in the small-set sense that every nonempty X ⊆ L with |X| ≤ s satisfies |N(X)| ≥ (d - 1)|X| + 1. Then the binary Tanner code B(G) defined by the right-side parity checks has minimum Hamming distance at least s + 1; equivalently, every codeword x ∈ B(G) whose support has size at most s is the zero word.
domain_bridges: finite bipartite graph combinatorics -> parity-check linear codes over ZMod 2
proof_strategy: Let X be the support of a nonzero codeword of weight at most s. By s-optimality, |N(X)| ≥ (d - 1)|X| + 1. Because x satisfies all right parity checks over F₂, every right vertex in N(X) is adjacent to at least two vertices of X. Hence the number of edges between X and N(X) is at least 2|N(X)|. Left d-regularity gives exactly d|X| such edges. Combining yields d|X| ≥ 2((d - 1)|X| + 1), i.e. 0 ≥ (d - 2)|X| + 2, impossible for d ≥ 2. Therefore X is empty.
title: S-optimal Tanner graphs have no binary codewords of weight at most s

description: For every fixed integer k >= 2, the normalized excess g_k(n) / log n converges in natural density to the binary upper-bound constant (k - 1) / log 2. Equivalently, for every epsilon > 0, the proportion of n <= x for which |g_k(n) / log n - (k - 1) / log 2| > epsilon tends to 0 as x tends to infinity.
domain_bridges: factorial divisibility to p-adic valuation inequalities
binary digit sums to carries in addition
density-one asymptotics to filter convergence over finite counting measures
proof_strategy: Use Legendre's formula to translate a_1! ... a_k! | n! into simultaneous digit-sum inequalities. The paper proves the upper bound from the binary digit-sum obstruction and a density-one lower bound from mixed 2--3 rarefaction. The conjectural strengthening is that the binary obstruction is asymptotically sharp for almost all n. A proof would likely construct, for almost every n, admissible tuples a_i whose total excess is ((k - 1) / log 2 - o(1)) log n, while controlling all odd-prime valuation constraints by showing that the binary carry construction can be locally repaired at negligible logarithmic cost.
title: Binary Leading Constant for the Almost-Everywhere Size of Factorial Excess

Lee--Szczarba vanishing of top rational cohomology of SL_n(Z)
Theorems A and B of the given paper: codimension-one and codimension-two vanishing for Gamma_{0,n}(p)

The Hecke congruence condition can be encoded as the stabilizer of a line in F_p^n, linking arithmetic subgroups of SL_n(Z) to finite projective geometry over F_p.
A Lean formalization would bridge group cohomology, integer matrix groups, finite-index subgroups, and rational vector-space vanishing.

The expected new input is a strengthened acyclicity range for the relevant sharbly or partial-frame complex modulo the Hecke congruence action, together with explicit control of stabilizer homology in degrees at most 3. The conjectural linear bound 10p+11 continues the observed codimension-one and codimension-two pattern 4p+5, 7p+8.
title: Codimension-three rational cohomology of Hecke congruence subgroups vanishes in a linear stable range

description: Let Σ be a finite connected signed simple graph, let v be a non-isolated vertex, and let ρ(Σ) denote the spectral radius of its signed adjacency matrix. The paper proves ρ(Σ)^2 ≤ ρ(Σ - v)^2 + 2 d(v) - 1. Conjecture: equality holds if and only if either the underlying unsigned graph is a star and v is a pendant vertex, or the underlying unsigned graph is complete and the signing is balanced or antibalanced.
domain_bridges: signed graphs as symmetric real matrices
Perron-Frobenius comparison with the unsigned adjacency matrix
proof_strategy: First formalize signed simple graphs as symmetric {−1,0,1}-valued adjacency matrices over a finite vertex type, with deletion as principal submatrix restriction. Prove the vertex-deletion inequality using the block-matrix spectral-radius lemma from the paper. For equality, trace equality through the block estimate and through |A(Σ)| ≤ A(G). Show that equality forces the underlying unsigned graph to be one of the unsigned extremal cases of Sun-Das: a star with v pendant or a complete graph. In the star case every signing is switching-equivalent on a tree, so equality follows. In the complete case, prove that a signed complete graph on n vertices has spectral radius n−1 exactly when its signing is balanced or antibalanced, equivalently switching-equivalent to the all-positive or all-negative complete graph.
title: Equality cases for signed vertex-deletion spectral-radius bound

catalog_references: Chvatal 1977 tree versus clique Ramsey numbers
description: For every finite tree T and every integer k >= 2 with part sizes 1 <= m_1 <= ... <= m_k, the Ramsey number of T against the complete k-partite graph K_{m_1,...,m_k} is at most (k-1)(R(T,K_{m_1,m_2})-1)+m_1. This removes the sufficiently-large-tree hypothesis from the main theorem of the paper. It is falsifiable by a single explicit finite tree T, parameter tuple (m_1,...,m_k), and red-blue coloring on the claimed number of vertices avoiding both a red T and a blue K_{m_1,...,m_k}.
domain_bridges: Ramsey theory to extremal graph theory via Burr-type canonical colorings
complete multipartite graph structure to finite type-indexed graph formalization
asymptotic combinatorics to exact finite combinatorics
proof_strategy: Try to combine the paper's asymptotic argument with a finite obstruction analysis. First formalize Burr's lower-bound coloring and the monotonicity of Ramsey numbers. Then reduce a minimal counterexample to a red graph whose connected components all have order less than |T| and whose blue complement avoids the required multipartite graph. Analyze the component-size profile: if at least k-1 components have near-|T| capacity, use the bipartite bound R(T,K_{m_1,m_2}) to force the first two blue parts; otherwise use the total vertex count to force a reservoir of size at least m_1. Remaining finite exceptional profiles could in principle be discharged by exact inequalities on component capacities rather than regularity.
title: Finite Erdős-550 Ramsey Upper Bound Without the Large-Tree Hypothesis

description: For every integer base b ≥ 2 and every t ≥ 1, let s_b(n) be the sum of the base-b digits of n. The limiting density, computed along complete radix intervals [0, b^k), of n such that s_b(n+t) ≥ s_b(n) exists and is strictly greater than 1/2. Equivalently, the sequence (# {0 ≤ n < b^k : s_b(n+t) ≥ s_b(n)} / b^k) converges to a real c_{b,t} with c_{b,t} > 1/2. A counterexample would be a pair (b,t) with b ≥ 2, t ≥ 1 for which this limit fails to exist or is ≤ 1/2.
domain_bridges: finite-state carry automata for addition by a fixed integer
radix digit-sum distributions as stationary measures of Markov chains
binary Cusick inequality as the b = 2 specialization
stopped random-walk laws for carry propagation
proof_strategy: Generalize the paper's deconvolution from binary carries to base-b carries. Model addition by t on the first k radix digits as a finite carry automaton with an absorbing tail once all digits of t and all carries vanish. Express s_b(n+t)-s_b(n) as a finite additive functional of this automaton plus a geometrically distributed carry-propagation tail. Then prove a first-exit median or reflection-type inequality for the resulting stopped walk showing that the nonnegative half-line has mass strictly larger than 1/2. The Lean formalization can avoid natural density by working with the radix interval limits over b^k.
title: Base-b Cusick Bias for Sum-of-Digits Increments

description: For every integer k ≥ 2, there exists an open interval I_k ⊂ (0,1) such that for all β ∈ I_k, the minimum fixed-density semi-inducibility of the red-blue star S_{k,1} (with k red edges and 1 blue edge from a distinguished center) at density β strictly exceeds min(β^k(1−β), β(1−β)^k), the envelope formed by the quasi-clique and quasi-star constructions. This generalizes the paper's result for S_{2,1}, where the true minimum is given by a three-class complement-split family rather than the natural quasi-star/quasi-clique endpoint profile on an interval around β = 1/2. For S_{k,1}, the conjectured minimizer is a step-function graphon with at most k+1 classes.
proof_strategy: Extend the paper's transfer argument with degree-power tie-breaking to the functional f_k(d) = d(d−1)⋯(d−k+1)(n−1−d). Reduce the graphon variational problem to almost-regular, threshold, and finite-staircase optimizations. Show that any graphon achieving the quasi-star/quasi-clique envelope can be perturbed into a (k+1)-class complement-split graphon that strictly decreases the S_{k,1} density at the same edge density, using a Lagrangian comparison on the class-structured ansatz. The key step is proving that the complement-split family dominates the envelope on an interval whose width grows with k.
title: Complement-split minima exceed the quasi-star/quasi-clique envelope for semi-induced stars S_{k,1}

description: In the wall version of Menger's theorem (Theorem 1 of the paper), the separator bound f can be taken to equal s' - 1, matching the classical Menger bound. Specifically: for all positive integers s' and t', there exists an integer t such that for any vertex set A and any wall W of size at least t, either there exists a vertex set X of size at most s' - 1 that separates A from the branch vertices of W, or there exists a subwall W' of size at least t' together with s' vertex-disjoint A-W'-paths each ending in a distinct nail of W'.
proof_strategy: Attempt to prove f = s' - 1 suffices by adapting the classical Menger argument to walls: if no separator of size s' - 1 exists between A and the branch vertices of W, then by Menger's theorem there are s' disjoint paths from A to the branch vertices. The challenge is controlling where these paths attach in W. Use the flat wall theorem and the hierarchical structure of subwalls to reroute paths so they end in distinct nails of a suitable subwall W'. A counterexample strategy would construct a wall where many A-W paths must converge on the same nail of every large subwall.
title: Wall-Menger Separator Optimality Conjecture

description: The specific degree one function on the Grassmann scheme $J_3(4,2)$ defined by $f = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{Q(p) = 0} x_p + \frac{1}{6} \sum_{Q(p) = 1} x_p - \frac{1}{6} \sum_{Q(p) = 2} x_p$, where $Q(x,y,z,w) = x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - w^2$ is an elliptic quadric over $\mathbb{F}_3$, is Boolean and not a trivial Boolean degree one function.
proof_strategy: Define the Grassmannian $J_3(4,2)$ and the Bruen-Drudge function $f$ over $\mathbb{F}_3^4$. Prove $f$ is Boolean by classifying the 2-dimensional subspaces (lines) and showing the weight distribution of $Q$ on each line restricts to one of $(2,1,1)$, $(1,3,0)$, $(1,0,3)$, or $(0,2,2)$, which evaluates $f$ to either 0 or 1. Prove $f$ is non-trivial by demonstrating its coefficients do not match the coefficient patterns of any of the 8 trivial templates.
title: Non-triviality of the Bruen-Drudge Boolean degree one function on $J_3(4,2)$

description: For every natural number n ≥ 1, the number of 2-binomial equivalence classes of binary words of length n equals the n-th cake number: |{0,1}^n / ∼₂| = (n³ + 5n + 6)/6 = Σ_{r=0}^{3} C(n,r). Two words u,v ∈ {0,1}* are 2-binomially equivalent if for every word w of length at most 2, the binomial coefficient (u choose w) = (v choose w), where (u choose w) counts scattered subword occurrences of w in u. This identity, first proved by Rigo and Salimov (2015), connects the algebraic structure of k-binomial equivalence on words to the enumerative geometry of hyperplane arrangements in ℝ³ via the Steiner-Schläfli formula.
proof_strategy: Define word binomial coefficients (u choose w) counting scattered subword occurrences, define 2-binomial equivalence ∼₂, show that for binary words of length n the equivalence is determined by the triple (|u|_a, (u choose ab), (u choose ba)) subject to the constraints |u|_a + |u|_b = n and (u choose ab) + (u choose ba) = |u|_a · |u|_b, then establish a bijection between valid triples and chambers of the associated hyperplane arrangement in ℝ³, and count these chambers via the Steiner-Schläfli formula to obtain the cake number.
title: Binary 2-binomial equivalence class count equals cake number

description: The original theorem characterizes $D(k) = \gcd_{2\leq q\leq k+1} \binom{qk}{k} = 1$ based on the largest prime-power component of $n=k+1$. We propose a generalization: For fixed $k \geq 2$ and a step size $s \geq 1$, define $D(k, s) = \gcd_{j=1}^{\lfloor (k+1)/s \rfloor} \binom{(js)k}{k}$. The conjecture is that $D(k, s) = 1$ if and only if for every prime power $p^a \parallel n=k+1$, the condition $n/p^a > p^a$ is modified by a factor dependent on $s$, specifically involving the p-adic valuation of $s$.
proof_strategy: Extend the finite-difference argument to show that any prime divisor of $D(k, s)$ must divide $s(k+1)$. Use Lucas' Theorem to analyze the p-adic carry behavior of $\binom{qsk}{k}$ and apply the digit-box stabilizer method to determine the conditions under which the gcd remains 1, specifically examining the interaction between the base-$p$ expansions of $s$ and $k$.
title: Generalization of the Binomial GCD Criterion for Arithmetic Progressions of Upper Indices

description:
For a finite group \(\Gamma\) and any non‑negative function \(f:\Gamma\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), define the two‑sided correlation kernel \(\mathcal C_f\) by
\[\mathcal C_f(x,y)=\frac{1}{|\Gamma|}\sum_{a_1,a_2\in\Gamma:\, xa_1=a_2 y} f(a_1)f(a_2) = \mathbb{E}_{z\in\Gamma} f(x^{-1}z)f(zy^{-1}).\]
The conjecture asserts that \(\mathcal C_f\) satisfies Sidorenko’s inequality for **all** finite (undirected) bipartite graphs \(H\):
\[ t(H,\mathcal C_f) \ge t(K_2,\mathcal C_f)^{e(H)}. \]
Equivalently, the homomorphism density of any bipartite graph in \(\mathcal C_f\) is at least the \(e(H)\)-th power of the edge density of \(\mathcal C_f\). This extends the theorem of the paper, which proves the statement only for directed graphs (or for the 1‑subdivision of any directed graph). The conjecture is precise and falsifiable: a single counterexample \((\Gamma,f,H)\) with \(t(H,\mathcal C_f)<t(K_2,\mathcal C_f)^{e(H)}\) disproves it.
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by adapting the entropy‑based proof of Sidorenko for trees and strongly tree‑decomposable graphs to the kernel \(\mathcal C_f\). One promising route is to view \(\mathcal C_f\) as the convolution \(f * f^{\mathrm{rev}}\) on the group algebra, where \(f^{\mathrm{rev}}(g)=f(g^{-1})\). The edge density is then \(\|f\|_1^2/|\Gamma|^2\). For a bipartite graph \(H\) with a tree‑like decomposition, one can iteratively apply Hölder’s inequality together with the invariance of \(\mathcal C_f\) under left and right translations to obtain the desired lower bound. A second line of attack uses the graphon formalism: embed \(\mathcal C_f\) as a step‑function graphon and invoke the known validity of Sidorenko for step‑graphons that are products of a function and its reverse. Formalizing either route in Lean would provide a mechanised proof or a counterexample via exhaustive search on small groups.
title: Sidorenko Property for Two‑Sided Correlation Kernels on Finite Groups

description: Let (a_k)_{k ≥ 1} be the Pólya tree enumeration sequence with ordinary generating function A(z) = Σ_{k≥1} a_k z^k satisfying A(z) = z·exp(A(z))·Φ(z) where Φ(z) = exp(Σ_{i≥2} A(z^i)/i). Define ω_k = Σ_{d|k} d·a_d. Then a_1 = 1 and for all k ≥ 2, a_k = (1/(k-1))·Σ_{j=1}^{k-1} a_j·ω_{k-j}.
proof_strategy: Define Pólya trees via the functional equation A(z) = z·exp(A(z))·Φ(z) as a formal power series. Differentiate both sides to obtain z·A'(z) = A(z)·(1 + Σ_{i≥1} z^i·A'(z^i)). Extract the coefficient of z^k on both sides. The inner sum Σ_{i≥1} z^i·A'(z^i) has coefficient [z^k] = Σ_{d|k} d·a_d = ω_k by collecting terms where i·j = k with j indexing powers of A'. The left side gives k·a_k and the right side gives a_k + Σ_{j=1}^{k-1} a_j·ω_{k-j}, yielding the recurrence after rearrangement.
title: Pólya tree coefficient recurrence formula

description: For a number field k with r₁ real and r₂ complex places, let b = r₁·⌊n²/4⌋ + r₂·n(n-1)/2. For any cohomological generic representation π in R_ε^{coge,∞} of GL(n,k_∞) with coefficient system F_π and quadratic character ε: π₀(k_∞×) → ℂ×, the Betti-Whittaker period of the contragredient π∨ in degree b satisfies P^b(π∨, F_{π∨}, ε) = ε(disc(k))^b · P^b(π, F_π, ε), where disc(k) is viewed as an element of π₀(k_∞×) via the determinant identification π₀(k_∞×) ≅ π₀(GL_n(k_∞)).
proof_strategy: First formalize the cohomological generic representations of GL(n) over number fields, define the bottom-degree Betti-Whittaker period functional via continuous group cohomology H^b_ct(GL_n(k_∞)⁰; F_π ⊗ π) → ℂ through the Whittaker pairing, establish the identification π₀(k_∞×) ≅ π₀(GL_n(k_∞)) via determinant, then prove the period relation by extending Chen's argument using the functional equation framework and the Casselman-Wallach module structure on the Whittaker model.
title: Betti-Whittaker Period Relation for Contragredient Representations of GL(n)

description: For the imaginary quadratic field K = Q(i), the automorphism group of a very general S_K(2)-polarized K3 surface X_{K,2} is isomorphic to the projective principal congruence subgroup of level 2 of the Bianchi group PGL_2(O_K). Specifically, Aut(X_{Q(i),2}) ≅ PΓ_{Q(i)}(2).
proof_strategy: Construct explicit double-cover models of the K3 surface from the Kummer surface Km(E_K x E_K). Compute the Néron-Severi lattice to show it is isometric to S_K(2). Prove that the representation of the automorphism group on the Néron-Severi lattice is injective, and explicitly match the automorphisms to the generators of the level-2 projective congruence subgroup via their geometric actions (deck involutions and Mordell-Weil translations).
title: Exact Realization of Level-2 Bianchi Congruence Subgroups as K3 Surface Automorphisms over Q(i)

description: Every connected, twin-free Cayley digraph of a finite abelian group is stable, i.e., for such a digraph G, Aut(G × K₂) = Aut(G) × Aut(K₂). This extends the paper's result (Theorem 1.3) which proves nonexistence of nontrivially unstable Cayley digraphs of abelian groups of odd order to all finite abelian groups, resolving the even order case that remains open.
domain_bridges: Graph theory (digraphs, direct products, automorphism groups)
proof_strategy: Use the paper's necessary and sufficient condition for instability of connected digraphs to reduce the problem to ruling out the existence of certain automorphism structures in Cayley digraphs of even-order abelian groups. Leverage the algebraic regularity of Cayley digraphs and the structure theorem for finite abelian groups to show that the twin-free condition and connectedness preclude any additional automorphisms in G × K₂ beyond the product action.
title: Stability of Cayley Digraphs of Abelian Groups

description: For every SIC dimension d with base quadratic field K = Q(√Δ₀), and for every Weyl-Heisenberg SIC overlap unit ε (the absolute value of a mutual scalar product of distinct SIC vectors), there exist Stark units η₁, ..., ηₖ of the ray class field K^{fd∞₁} (where f is the conductor dividing f₀(d)) and integers n₁, ..., nₖ such that ε = ∏ᵢ ηᵢ^{nᵢ/2}. In the minimal case (f = 1), the Stark units belong to K^{d∞₁} attached to the maximal ring of integers; in the non-minimal case, a lattice of ray class fields K_L^{d;f} is involved. This unifies the observed algebraic structure of SIC overlaps with Stark's conjectures and the Shintani–Faddeev modular cocycle.
proof_strategy: First verify computationally for all known SIC dimensions d ≤ 193 that overlap units decompose as claimed using explicit Stark unit computations in ray class fields. Then leverage the Shintani–Faddeev modular cocycle to establish the decomposition analytically: show that the cocycle values producing overlap phases coincide with the Stark unit valuations predicted by the rank-1 abelian Stark conjecture. The non-minimal case requires tracking the lattice of conductors f | f₀ and showing that each K_L^{d;f} embeds appropriately into K^{fd∞₁}. The ±1 phenomenon in alternate dimensions follows from proving that certain ray class fields have Stark units of norm ±1, which constrains the overlap phases.
title: SIC Overlap Units are Products of Square Roots of Stark Units

description: Let G be a simple left d-regular bipartite graph with d ≥ 2 and girth at least 2k + 2. Then the minimum distance of the binary linear code B(G) is at least k + 1. This connects the combinatorial structure of optimal small-set expanders (characterized by girth) to the coding-theoretic properties of their associated codes, which is central to the paper's application to post-quantum key exchange.
proof_strategy: By contradiction: assume a codeword x ∈ B(G) of Hamming weight w with 1 ≤ w ≤ k. Let S = supp(x). Since girth ≥ 2k + 2 ≥ 2w + 2, the induced subgraph on S ∪ N(S) is acyclic (any cycle has length ≤ 2w < 2k + 2). In this forest, each vertex in S has degree d (left-regularity) and each vertex in N(S) has even degree ≥ 2 (parity-check condition from x ∈ B(G)). Degree-sum gives d|S| = Σ_{v∈N(S)} deg(v) ≥ 2|N(S)|, so |N(S)| ≤ d|S|/2. But the forest property gives d|S| = edges ≤ vertices − 1 = |S| + |N(S)| − 1, so |N(S)| ≥ (d−1)|S| + 1. Combining yields (d−1)|S| + 1 ≤ d|S|/2, i.e., (d−2)|S|/2 ≤ −1, contradicting d ≥ 2 and |S| ≥ 1.
title: Girth bounds minimum distance of bipartite graph codes

description: For the full flag variety GL_{n+1}/ℂ B, let w ∈ S_{n+1} index the Schubert cell X_w^o. The cluster algebra structure on ℂ[X_w^o] (coming from the reduced expression of the longest element in the Weyl group modulo the stabilizer of w) is of finite type if and only if w is a Grassmannian permutation (i.e., w has at most one descent).
proof_strategy: Show that the exchange matrix associated to a reduced word for w is mutation-equivalent to a Cartesian product of type A_{k_i} cluster algebras exactly when the corresponding permutation has at most one descent, using the correspondence between reduced words and pipe dreams, and applying known classification of finite type cluster algebras via Dynkin diagrams. Conversely, if w has ≥2 descents, exhibit a mutable vertex whose mutation creates a cycle of length >2, preventing finite type.
title: Finite type of cluster algebras on Schubert cells in type A flag varieties

description: For integers d≥2 and n≥2d+2, the maximum size M_d(n) of a (d+1)-uniform family on [n] with VC‑dimension at most d equals the maximum, over 0≤k≤⌊d/2⌋, of the sum of binomial coefficients Σ_{i=0}^k binom{n-2i-1}{d-2i}. This quantity is attained by the “layered star” construction that takes all (d+1)-subsets containing a fixed element and, for each i≤k, also all (d+1)-subsets containing a second fixed element and missing exactly i additional prescribed points. The conjecture refines the Ahlswede–Khachatrian bound and predicts the exact extremal families for all d and n.
proof_strategy: Show that any (d+1)-uniform family F⊆[n]^{(d+1)} with VC(F)≤d can be transformed, via a sequence of shifting operations that preserve VC-dimension, into a layered star without decreasing its size. Then prove that a layered star of parameter k has size Σ_{i=0}^k binom{n-2i-1}{d-2i} and that no larger layered star exists. The upper bound follows from a double‑counting argument on shattered sets together with induction on n, using the Sauer–Shelah lemma for the lower layers. Formalisation in Lean proceeds by encoding families as finite sets of finsets, defining VC‑dimension, implementing shifting lemmas, and proving the size formula by combinatorial identities.
title: A Sharp Upper Bound for Uniform VC‑Dimension Families via Layered Stars

description: For a connected signed graph Σ and a non-isolated vertex v, the inequality λ₁(Σ) ≤ √(λ₁²(Σ−v) + 2d(v) − 1) holds, with equality if and only if Σ is a signed star with v as the center or Σ is a signed complete graph.
proof_strategy: Use eigenvalue interlacing inequalities and structural analysis of signed graphs. Leverage Rayleigh quotient bounds and properties of signed stars/complete graphs to characterize equality conditions.
title: Equality Cases for Spectral Radius Bound in Signed Graphs

catalog_references: Maclagan-Sturmfels, Introduction to Tropical Geometry, Theorem 4.6.8: Tropical Bernstein theorem
Esterov-Gusev classification of tuples of lattice polytopes of mixed volume one
description: For every full-dimensional lattice polytope P in Z^n, let Sigma_P be the tropical hypersurface given by the codimension-one skeleton of the normal fan of P, with edge-length weights. The n-fold stable self-intersection Sigma_P ∩_st ... ∩_st Sigma_P is a reduced point at the origin if and only if P is a unimodular simplex, equivalently if and only if the normalized lattice volume n! vol(P) is equal to 1.
domain_bridges: Tropical stable intersection multiplicity is converted to mixed volume via tropical Bernstein.
The unmixed mixed volume MV(P,...,P) is the normalized lattice volume n! vol(P).
A full-dimensional lattice polytope has normalized volume one exactly when it is unimodularly equivalent to the standard simplex.
proof_strategy: First formalize lattice polytopes in Z^n, Euclidean volume, normalized volume, mixed volume, and the normal-fan tropical hypersurface Sigma_P. Use the tropical Bernstein theorem to identify the weight of the n-fold stable intersection of Sigma_P with MV(P,...,P). Prove algebraically from the definition of mixed volume that MV(P,...,P) = n! * vol(P). Finally prove the discrete convex-geometric lemma that a full-dimensional lattice polytope has normalized volume one iff its lattice points are exactly the vertices of an affine unimodular image of the standard simplex. Combining these equivalences gives the iff statement.
title: Unmixed Reduced Tropical Bernstein Criterion

description: Every ⊆-minimal minor-closed graph class with limiting density greater than some δ < 3/2 can be characterized by excluding a single graph as a minor. Formally, for any such class 𝒢, there exists a graph H such that 𝒢 = excl({H}).
proof_strategy: Leverage the Robertson-Seymour theorem on finite forbidden minors and the paper's classification of minimal classes to show that the minimal sets of forbidden graphs for these classes must be singletons.
title: Minimal Minor-Closed Classes Below 3/2 Have Single Forbidden Minors

description: For all integers n ≥ (s+1)k and a prime power q, the maximum cardinality m_q(n,k,s) of a family of k‑dimensional subspaces of an n‑dimensional vector space over 𝔽_q with no s+1 members whose sum is direct equals the larger of the two natural constructions: all k‑subspaces contained in a ((s+1)k−1)‑dimensional subspace, or all k‑subspaces intersecting a fixed s‑dimensional subspace nontrivially.
proof_strategy: Apply Lovász's matroid matching minimax theorem, a high-dimensional Hoffman bound for uniform hypergraphs, and vector-space packing-design arguments to prove the equality.
title: Exactevaluation of the vector-space Erdős Matching number m_q(n,k,s)

description: The main theorem of the paper proves that for fixed integers k ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ m₁ ≤ … ≤ m_k, there exists n₀ = n₀(m₁,…,m_k) such that for every n ≥ n₀ and every n-vertex tree T, R(T, K_{m₁,…,m_k}) ≤ (k-1)(R(T, K_{m₁,m₂}) - 1) + m₁. We conjecture that the 'sufficiently large' condition can be removed entirely: the inequality holds for all trees T (i.e., for all n ≥ 1).
proof_strategy: Attempt to adapt the off-Turán embedding and compactness-rounding arguments to eliminate the dependence on n₀. Alternatively, perform a systematic case analysis for small n using structural properties of trees and known exact Ramsey numbers for small complete multipartite graphs.
title: Erdős Problem 550 for All Trees

description: For any integer $i \geq 0$ and prime $p$, there exists a constant $C_i$ such that the rational cohomology of the Hecke congruence subgroup $\Gamma_{0,n}(p)$ vanishes in codimension $i$ for all $n \geq C_i p$. This extends the paper's results which prove this for $i=0,1,2$ with bounds $n \geq \frac{p+14}{6}$, $n \geq 4p+5$, and $n \geq 7p+8$ respectively.
proof_strategy: Establish a uniform linear bound by inducting on the codimension $i$, utilizing Borel-Serre duality to relate high-degree cohomology to low-degree homology, and carefully controlling the $p$-torsion dependencies in the spectral sequence of the complex of apartments.
title: Linear Vanishing Bound for Hecke Congruence Subgroup Cohomology

catalog_references: Lattice basis reduction in Diophantine equations
description: Conjecture: For every natural number n > 7, the equation n! + 1 = m^2 has no integer solution m. In other words, the only solutions to the Brocard problem are the three known Brown pairs (4,5), (5,11), and (7,71).
proof_strategy: Use a combination of modular arithmetic to rule out congruence classes mod small primes, p‑adic valuation to show that n! + 1 cannot be a square when n exceeds 7, and LLL lattice reduction to bound possible m via approximations of sqrt(n!+1). The strategy involves proving that for any n > 7, there exists a prime p > 7 such that v_p(n!) is odd, which forces n! + 1 to be congruent to 1 mod p but not a quadratic residue modulo p. This approach would be formalized by iteratively eliminating admissible n using explicit bounds from the Chebyshev theta function and explicit factorial bounds, culminating in a contradiction for each n > 7.
title: Non‑existence of Further Brown Numbers Beyond n=7

catalog_references: Erdős–Graham (1980) – monograph on products of factorials
description: Conjecture that the constants in the known bounds for $g_k(n)$ are best possible. For each $k\ge2$, the liminf of $g_k(n)/\log n$ equals $3(k-1)/\log12$ and the limsup equals $(k-1)/\log2$. Equivalently, any larger lower constant fails on a set of density 1 and any smaller upper constant fails on a set of density 1.
domain_bridges: Analytic number theory ↔ Combinatorial number theory
proof_strategy: To prove the conjecture one would need to show that the existing lower‑bound machinery (uniform phase separation on $S$‑unit progressions and digit‑sum normal order) already forces the liminf to be at most $3(k-1)/\log12$, while a refined Kummer‑sieve combined with mixed $2$–$3$ representations can produce infinitely many $n$ attaining the upper constant $(k-1)/\log2$, thereby establishing the limsup. Conversely, any improvement of the lower constant would contradict the density‑zero exceptional set obtained from the digit‑sum normal order theorem.
title: Optimality of the density‑one lower and pointwise upper bounds for Erdős Problem 400

description: Conjecture that for all integers t ≥ 2 and m ≥ 1, if nonzero linear forms ℓ₁,…,ℓ_t over a field of characteristic zero have m-th powers ℓ₁^m,…,ℓ_t^m that are minimally linearly dependent, then dim Span{ℓ₁,…,ℓ_t} ≤ (t + m - 2)/m, with equality if and only if the linear forms are linearly dependent in a way that their supports form a rational normal curve in the Veronese embedding.
proof_strategy: Leverage coding-theoretic translation where the coefficient row space of the powers is the m-th Schur power of the coefficient code, then apply the Schur-product Kneser theorem of Mirandola and Zémor to derive the dimension bound.
title: Sharp dimension bound for minimal dependencies of linear-form powers in Veronese circuits

catalog_references: Euler characteristic additivity for finite CW-complex decompositions
Multiplicativity of Euler characteristic under finite CW products
Smith normal form for rank-one integer matrices
Homotopy type of (C*)^n as the real n-torus (S^1)^n
De Concini-Procesi theory of toric arrangements
description: Let A be any finite parallel toric arrangement in (C*)^n, defined by nonzero rank-one integral characters and constants in C*. If n >= 2, then the Euler-Poincare characteristic of the complement M(A) is zero. Equivalently, deleting any finite family of pairwise disjoint parallel hypertori from a complex algebraic torus of dimension at least two does not change the vanishing Euler characteristic of the ambient torus.
domain_bridges: Use Smith normal form over Z to reduce a rank-one toric arrangement to equations x_1^d = beta_i.
Identify the complement up to finite covering or homotopy as (C* \ D) x (C*)^(n-1), where D is finite.
Apply multiplicativity of Euler characteristic and chi(C*) = 0 when n >= 2.
Translate the topological statement into a Lean formalization using an abstract EulerPoincare invariant satisfying finite-CW product and additivity properties.
proof_strategy: First show that all defining exponent vectors of a parallel rank-one arrangement are integer multiples of one primitive vector. By a GL_n(Z) monomial change of coordinates, send this primitive vector to the first coordinate. Each hypertorus is then a union of fibers of x_1^d = beta_i, so the complement is homotopy equivalent, up to a finite disjoint union/finite covering that preserves the zero conclusion, to (C* minus finitely many points) times (C*)^(n-1). Since n >= 2, the second factor contains C*, whose Euler-Poincare characteristic is zero. Multiplicativity of Euler characteristic gives chi(M(A)) = chi(C* \ D) * chi((C*)^(n-1)) = chi(C* \ D) * 0 = 0.
title: Vanishing of Euler characteristic for higher-dimensional parallel toric arrangement complements

description: For tensor-product function spaces with a worst-case function h satisfying specific integrality and sparsity conditions, the information complexity for non-negative linear rules exhibits a curse of dimensionality.
proof_strategy: Construct a family of functions leveraging the worst-case h and s_y to show exponential lower bounds via combinatorial arguments.
title: Exponential Information Complexity in Tensor-Product Function Spaces

description: Find an Euler brick whose space diagonal is also an integer, or prove none exists. Formalize the parametric families of near-misses and connect to Diophantine equations on algebraic surfaces.
title: Perfect Cuboid (Euler Brick)

description: Extend results on quadratic forms to arbitrary algebraic number fields. Formalize the Hasse-Minkowski theorem and explore the classification of quadratic forms over number fields via class field theory.
title: Hilbert 11: Quadratic Forms over Algebraic Fields

description: Prove that for every finite union-closed family of sets (not all empty), some element belongs to at least half the sets. Formalize the lattice-theoretic reformulation and known partial results.
title: Frankl's Union-Closed Conjecture

description: Characterize numbers representable as a sum of three squares of primes. Formalize the circle method approach to ternary Goldbach-type problems for squares.
title: Legendre's Three-Square Theorem Extension

description: Prove that for every polynomial with all roots in the closed unit disk, every root has a critical point within distance 1 of it. Formalize known partial results and the connection to Gauss-Lucas.
title: Sendov's Conjecture

description: Formalize the Euler-Mascheroni constant γ = lim(H_n - ln n). Prove key integral representations and series accelerations. Establish Apéry-like sequences that provide good rational approximations. Explore connections to the Stieltjes constants.
title: Euler-Mascheroni Constant: Irrationality Approaches

title: Frankl's Union-Closed Conjecture: Partial Results

description: Determine whether Lehmer's polynomial has the smallest Mahler measure among non-cyclotomic polynomials. Formalize the Mahler measure and its connections to heights, entropy, and algebraic dynamics.
title: Lehmer's Mahler Measure Problem

description: Prove that every tree admits a graceful labeling. Formalize known results for paths, caterpillars, and olive trees. Explore connections to decompositions of complete graphs.
title: Graceful Tree Conjecture

description: Find a formula for the probability that two elements chosen uniformly at random generate the symmetric group S_n. Formalize known asymptotic results and connect to the theory of random permutations.
title: Symmetric Group Generation Probability

description: Resolve whether the general 7th-degree equation can be solved using functions of only 2 variables. Formalize Kolmogorov's superposition theorem and explore its implications for approximation theory.
title: Hilbert 13: 7th-Degree Equations via 2-Variable Functions

title: Erdős–Straus Conjecture

description:
# Future Directions — Primality Testing (AKS & Miller–Rabin)

Derived from this cycle's findings in `AKSCriterion.lean` and `MillerRabin.lean`.
Each conjecture is bold, falsifiable, and accompanied by the decisive insight and
a "why now?" justification.

## 1. Introspective-base AKS bound

**Conjecture.** There is an explicit polynomial bound `B(n)` (polylog in `n`)
such that: `n` is prime iff `(X + a)^n = X^n + a` in `(ZMod n)[X] / (X^r - 1)`
for all `1 ≤ a ≤ B(n)`, where `r = O((log n)^c)`. Formalizing this turns the
single-base criterion `aks_criterion` into the full deterministic
polynomial-time AKS algorithm.

The key insight is... the proven exact criterion `aks_criterion` already isolates
the obstruction (the inner coefficient `C(n,q)`); the remaining work is purely
the cyclotomic *order/coprime-base counting* that bounds how many bases are
needed once one quotients by `X^r - 1`.

**Why now?** With the freshman's-dream equivalence fully formalized (0 sorries)
and `not_dvd_choose_prime_dvd` in hand, the algebraic core is settled; the
outstanding piece is a self-contained counting argument that Mathlib's
cyclotomic and `orderOf` API can now support.

## 2. Monier–Rabin 1/4 error bound

**Conjecture.** For every odd composite `n > 9`, the number of Miller–Rabin
non-witnesses in `(ZMod n)ˣ` is at most `φ(n)/4`. Equivalently, the soundness
theorem `miller_rabin_sound` has a quantitative converse: composites have many
witnesses.

The key insight is... `sqrt_one_in_ZMod_prime` fails modulo a composite (there
are ≥ 4 square roots of `1` by CRT), and the strong-liar set is contained in a
proper subgroup of `(ZMod n)ˣ`; bounding that subgroup's index by `4` is the
whole game.

**Why now?** Soundness (the easy half) is verified; Mathlib's `ZMod.unitsEquiv`
CRT decomposition and subgroup-index lemmas make the proper-subgroup counting
tractable for the first time in this codebase.

## 3. AKS strictly dominates Fermat on every Carmichael number

**Conjecture.** For *every* Carmichael number `n` (not just `561`), the Fermat
congruence holds for all bases yet the AKS identity fails for some base coprime
to `n`; moreover the failing base can be taken to be the least prime factor's
co-factor. This generalizes `carmichael_561_fools_fermat_not_aks` to the entire
family A002997.

The key insight is... `aks_identity_imp_fermat` shows AKS ⇒ Fermat, and
`aks_criterion` shows AKS ⇔ primality, so AKS-failure is automatic for any
composite; the new content is identifying a *coprime* failing base uniformly via
Korselt's structure (`n` squarefree, `(p-1) ∣ (n-1)`).

**Why now?** The separation is already proved at `561` with a reusable mechanism
(contrapositive of `aks_criterion`); only Korselt's criterion needs to be
formalized to make the argument uniform over A002997.

## 4. Carmichael numbers are exactly the Fermat-universal composites

**Conjecture.** A composite `n` satisfies `∀ a, a^n ≡ a (mod n)` iff `n` is
squarefree and `(p-1) ∣ (n-1)` for every prime `p ∣ n` (Korselt's criterion),
and these are exactly the composites on which the Fermat test never detects
compositeness.

The key insight is... the universal Fermat congruence decomposes via CRT into
per-prime-power conditions, and `a^n ≡ a` modulo `p^k` for all `a` forces
`k = 1` and `(p-1) ∣ (n-1)` through the cyclic structure of `(ZMod p)ˣ`.

**Why now?** Our `native_decide` evidence already confirms the family begins
`561, 1105` (A002997); a structural Korselt proof would replace finite checks by
a general theorem and feed directly into Direction 3.

## 5. A `ZMod`-native fast modular-exponentiation tactic with a correctness theorem

**Conjecture.** A `csimp`-backed binary modular-exponentiation routine computes
`a^e mod n` with a kernel-checked correctness lemma `powMod a e n = a^e % n`,
fast enough to discharge Miller–Rabin / AKS instances by `decide` rather than
`native_decide`, removing the `Lean.ofReduceBool` dependency from results like
`carmichael_561_fools_fermat_not_aks`.

The key insight is... square-and-multiply is a fold over the binary digits of the
exponent; its correctness is a clean induction, and a `@[csimp]` replacement
keeps the kernel in charge (no `@[implemented_by]` trust gap).

**Why now?** The only non-`propext`/`Classical`/`Quot` axiom in this cycle is the
compiler-trust `Lean.ofReduceBool` from `native_decide`; a verified `powMod`
would let the Carmichael witness be checked by the kernel alone.

# Future Directions — GL(1) Langlands correspondence

Derived from this cycle's findings: the cyclotomic GL(1) correspondence is realizable as an
*explicit group isomorphism* `DirichletCharacter ℂ n ≃* (Gal(ℚ(ζₙ)/ℚ) →* ℂˣ)`
(`LanglandsGL1.langlandsGL1`), with arithmetic shadow `φ(n)`
(`card_galois_reps_eq_totient`) and a CRT-driven local–global factorization
(`HeckeFactorization.heckeFactorization`).

## Conjecture 1 — Conductor-graded refinement of the correspondence

Under `langlandsGL1`, a Dirichlet character of conductor exactly `d ∣ n` maps to a Galois
representation that factors through `Gal(ℚ(ζ_d)/ℚ)` (i.e. is trivial on `Gal(ℚ(ζₙ)/ℚ(ζ_d))`),
giving a *graded* isomorphism indexed by conductor.

- The key insight is... that the correspondence is not just a bijection of groups but is
  compatible with the filtration by conductor, so the bijection restricts to each conductor
  stratum and the inclusion `ℚ(ζ_d) ⊆ ℚ(ζₙ)` becomes inflation of representations.
- Why now? We already have the unconditional iso over ℚ and the CRT factorization
  (`heckeFactorization`); Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.conductor` and the cyclotomic tower
  `IsCyclotomicExtension` instances make the stratification statable and checkable today.

## Conjecture 2 — L-functions match across the correspondence

For a Dirichlet character `χ` and its Galois counterpart `ρ = langlandsGL1 χ`, the Dirichlet
L-function `L(s, χ)` equals the Artin L-function `L(s, ρ)` term by term as Euler products.

- The key insight is... that the *local* CRT factorization established here
  (`heckeFactorization`) is exactly the place-by-place decomposition that makes the two Euler
  products agree factor by factor, reducing global equality to a per-prime statement.
- Why now? The group isomorphism is in hand, so the analytic comparison is the only missing
  ingredient; Mathlib's `LSeries` / `DirichletCharacter` L-function development gives a target
  to match the Galois side against.

## Conjecture 3 — Functoriality of the count under the cyclotomic tower

The totient counts assemble into an exact statement: the natural restriction map
`(Gal(ℚ(ζₘₙ)/ℚ) →* ℂˣ) → (Gal(ℚ(ζₘ)/ℚ) →* ℂˣ)` is surjective with kernel of order `φ(mn)/φ(m)`,
mirroring the surjection `(ℤ/mnℤ)ˣ ↠ (ℤ/mℤ)ˣ`.

- The key insight is... that `card_galois_reps_eq_totient` upgrades from a cardinality identity
  to an exact sequence once the tower maps are made explicit, encoding how Hecke characters lift
  along the cyclotomic tower.
- Why now? Both endpoints are formalized (`card_galois_reps_eq_totient`), and the unit-group
  surjection `(ℤ/mnℤ)ˣ ↠ (ℤ/mℤ)ˣ` used in `unitsCRT` is precisely the map to dualize.

## Conjecture 4 — Real-place / sign data is invisible at GL(1) over ℚ

Every finite-order Hecke character of `ℚ` is determined by its restriction to `(ℤ/nℤ)ˣ`
together with a single sign at the archimedean place, and the GL(1) correspondence is a
bijection onto Galois characters once that sign (parity, `χ(-1) = ±1`) is recorded.

- The key insight is... that the only archimedean datum at GL(1) over ℚ is the parity
  `χ(-1)`, so the "infinite place" contributes exactly one bit, matching even/odd Dirichlet
  characters to representations distinguished by complex conjugation.
- Why now? `MulChar` already exposes `χ(-1)`, and our isomorphism makes the even/odd split a
  decidable invariant transported to the Galois side, so the refined bijection is checkable.

## Conjecture 5 — Beyond ℚ: ray class characters for imaginary quadratic fields

The same composite (`autEquivPow`-style reciprocity) ∘ (`mulEquivToUnitHom`) realizes the
GL(1) correspondence for any abelian extension with a computable Galois-to-ray-class iso,
starting with imaginary quadratic fields where CM theory supplies the analogue of `autEquivPow`.

- The key insight is... that the only field-specific input to our proof is the reciprocity
  isomorphism `Gal ≃* (class/unit group)`; everything downstream (`precompMulEquiv`,
  `homProdEquiv`, the totient count) is formal and field-agnostic.
- Why now? The ℚ proof isolates exactly the one arithmetic black box that must be supplied per
  field, turning "do CFT for K" into "produce one `MulEquiv`", a sharply scoped target.

description: Arrow's impossibility theorem states that no ranked voting system with 3+ alternatives can be Pareto efficient, non-dictatorial, and independent of irrelevant alternatives (IIA). Conjecture: Arrow's theorem is a curvature statement. The space of preference profiles is a Riemannian manifold M with the Fisher information metric. The social welfare function F: M -> M is a mapping from profiles to social preferences. Arrow's conditions translate to geometric conditions: (1) Pareto efficiency means F preserves the direction of unanimous preference (F is 'forward-looking'). (2) IIA means F is a local mapping (the social preference at x depends only on local information near x). (3) Non-dictatorial means F is not a projection onto a single voter's preference. Conjecture: the only smooth, local, forward-looking maps on a positively curved manifold are projections (dictatorships). This is because a positively curved manifold has the property that parallel transport around a small loop rotates vectors (Holonomy), and a local, forward-looking map must preserve this holonomy, which forces it to be a projection. Conjecture: the curvature of the preference space is related to the 'polarization' of the electorate: when preferences are polarized (bimodal), the curvature is positive (sphere-like), and Arrow's theorem applies. When preferences are unimodal (consensus), the curvature is zero (flat), and majority rule works. Test: compute the curvature of the preference space for synthetic election data and verify the connection to Arrow's theorem. Impact: Arrow's impossibility is a theorem of differential geometry. Voting is curved.
proof_strategy: Define the preference space M = L(S)^n where L(S) is the set of linear orders on the alternative set S = {1, ..., m}. M is a discrete space with |L(S)|^n = (m!)^n points. To make this a manifold, we smooth it: replace each ranking with a utility vector u_i in R^m (normalized to the simplex Delta^{m-1}). The preference space becomes M = (Delta^{m-1})^n (n voters, each with a utility vector on the simplex). The Fisher information metric on M: g_{ij}(u) = E[(d/d u_i) log p(x|u) * (d/d u_j) log p(x|u)]. For the multinomial distribution: g_{ij} = delta_{ij} / u_i (the Fisher-Rao metric on the simplex). The curvature of (Delta^{m-1}, g) is constant positive (it's a spherical geometry). Arrow's conditions on F: M -> M: (1) Pareto: F(u_1, ..., u_n) has the same sign as the sum of u_i's (forward-looking). (2) IIA: F is local, i.e., dF only depends on local information (F is a smooth map). (3) Non-dictatorial: F is not a projection pi_i: (u_1, ..., u_n) -> u_i. Theorem: on a positively curved manifold, any smooth local forward-looking map is a projection. Proof sketch: by the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, a map from a positively curved manifold to itself that preserves direction must be either the identity or a projection. The key: the holonomy group of (Delta^{m-1})^n is SO(m-1)^n, and a local map must commute with this holonomy, which forces it to be a projection. Test: for m=3 alternatives, compute the curvature of Delta^2 (which is constant positive = 1/2), and verify that local forward-looking maps are projections.
title: The Geometry of Consensus: Arrow's Theorem as Curvature

description: The key insight is that the Collatz map T(n) = n/2 if n even, 3n+1 if n odd, appears to be a one-way function: easy to compute forward (polynomial time), intractable to invert (finding a preimage requires exponential search). Conjecture: Under the assumption that the Collatz conjecture is true, the function f(a, n) = T^a(n) (a iterations starting from n) is a one-way function with security parameter a. The inversion problem — given (a, f(a,n)), find n — requires O(2^{a/log(a)}) steps. Why now: the Collatz map has been verified to converge for all n up to 2^68, providing empirical evidence for irreversibility. Test: prove that f(a,n) cannot be inverted in sub-exponential time under a reasonable computational model. Construct a collision-resistant hash function from iterated Collatz maps. Impact: a new class of cryptographic primitives based on dynamical systems irreversibility, not number-theoretic hardness.
proof_strategy: Define Collatz hash H_k(x) = T^k(x) mod 2^256. Prove collision resistance: if H_k(x) = H_k(y) for x != y, then T^k(x) = T^k(y) mod 2^256, requiring T to have a period dividing 2^256 within k steps — contradicting empirical data showing no Collatz period below 2^68. Prove preimage resistance: given z, finding x with H_k(x) = z requires trying O(2^{128}) preimages because each Collatz step is a 2-to-1 map on average. Formalize in Lean 4: define the Collatz hash and prove its basic properties.
